spec_run: 0.5.4 spec run, specced early against a moving HEAD while 0.5.3's waves land (seed §4, James 2026-10-23 'get it ready for build so whenever all these waves finish we have 0.5.4 done if we need to modify post 0.5.3'): five groups (FA scale: incremental resolution + watch A2, multi-repo watch, the memory budget, build-target graphs, org routing; FB embeddings in glia, the embedding gate and Engram's data; FC the goal-layer connector, the clarification queue, concept search, PR intent, placement; FD the §E / §D precision group, self-graph hygiene, one tier vocabulary, the edge-precision audit, rustfmt / rustdoc; FE agent before / after, the zero-install CLI, the skills move, the use-signal proposal), each a spec agent + an adversarial verifier writing a FINAL packet file; one integrator (this file: F0 wave 0, the FZ release docs and handoffs, the completeness critic's additions FC.24 and FD.67-FD.72, cross-group seams, text patches, wave simulation). A re-verify pass after 0.5.3's last close-out (reverify_054.md) checks every packet against the landed 0.5.3 tree before W0.

constraints.api: breaks ALLOWED when declared in the packet's breaking block (kinds none, qname_shape, node_id, edge_removal, cell_value, api_signature, format, cli_output, out_of_repo); undeclared breaks are defects. Consumers pin 0.5.4 exactly (glia-py==0.5.4 / =0.5.4).
constraints.ids: F0.1 allocates the release's only registry ids: node_kind GOAL_UNIT = 50, edge_category TRACES = 38, cell_type UNIT = 26 and IMPORT_BINDINGS = 27 (next free 51 / 39 / 28). Every other packet uses them by NAME. The build-target domain's ids live in its own crate (build-domain), not in code-domain. A scan of every packet for a raw new id (NodeKindId(5x), EdgeCategoryId(3[89]), CellTypeId(2[6-9])) finds them only in F0.1.
constraints.format: no .gmap FORMAT_VERSION change (stays 3) and MANIFEST_VERSION stays 2. New ON-DISK side files, none read by a build except where stated: `.glia/vectors.jsonl` rows gain text_hash (FB.2; the sidecar becomes query-time only, FB.3), `.glia/targets-snapshot/` (FA.15) and `.glia/graph/targets.gmap` (FA.18, a header-described container written by an answer, as timeline.gmap is), `.glia/vocab-snapshot/` (FB.13a), `.glia/gh-snapshot/` (FC.17a, self-gitignored), engram-export `<out>.vocab.jsonl` (FB.13d). The goal graph is ordinary graph content (GOAL_UNIT / TRACES / UNIT), and NavFact variants appended by FD packets live only in the bincode parse cache (FD.20's finding).
constraints.query_time: Every snapshot step (glia embed, vocab sync, gh sync, targets sync, history sync / calibrate) runs only when called, never inside a build; the build READS gh-snapshot (FC.18) and never syncs. Embedding and similarity rank, never decide presence: a FACT / DERIVED row is never promoted or hidden by a learned or similarity score (seed §B), and the lexical absence stays beside semantic rows.
constraints.determinism: No HashMap iteration reaches an output; ties by qname / (repo label, path) / candidate index, never NodeId (FD.22 removes the remaining RepoId-ordered tie-breaks). Embeddings are CPU-only for determinism (the text-hash cache).
constraints.pin: every consumer handoff (FZ.2) states the exact pin glia-py == 0.5.4 / crates =0.5.4; the version bump is the release step after FZ, never a packet; nothing is pushed, tagged or published until James walks the commits.
constraints.lock: The workspace Cargo.lock moves ONCE, in F0.2 (glia-embed with fastembed =4.9.1 optional, glia-build-domain, glia-parser-bazel); licences checked (all permissive). glia-py's and glia-engine's default trees gain no ONNX / tokenizers crate (features `embed` / `sem-eval` off by default); the CLI's default feature `embed` links ORT. engram-export/Cargo.lock moves in F0.2 and wherever a packet changes engram-export's deps (FB.13d: none expected). Hashed roots gain `build-domain` (F0.2).
constraints.gate: 0.5.3's rank gate (`bash scripts/rank-gate.sh check`, EG.3) runs at every close-out of a wave touching a ranked path; every packet that changes an answer's order names it in its acceptance; the close-out also gains `cargo fmt --check` (F0.5) and a rustdoc gate (FD.23b).
constraints.public: The repo is public: no packet, harness, fixture or doc carries a private project's specifics (Kina / quokka internals); evaluations run on public repos (the rank gate's snapshots, the agent run's six repos) or report aggregates only; ~/Code/webplatform is never used.
constraints.followups: Every followup a 0.5.4 wave raises finishes inside 0.5.4 (seed §0 / §4): after each wave whose close-out lists unrouted followups with no remaining owner, the session clusters them by file, specs each cluster as an F<group>.<n> packet with a fixture or test, schedules a follow-up wave, and repeats until a close-out lists none; FZ runs after the last.

packets.title: The dependency commit: three new workspace crates as doc-only skeletons - embed/ (glia-embed, fastembed =4.9.1 OPTIONAL behind feature `fastembed`), build-domain/ (glia-build-domain) and parsers/build/bazel/ (glia-parser-bazel) - their manifest edges into engine / snapshots / cli / py with the heavy embedding stack feature-gated, `build-domain` in stamp's HASHED_ROOTS, and the release's one Cargo.lock change, licence-checked
packets.area: F0 - crates and dependencies
packets.rationale: CRATE / DEPENDENCY REQUESTS read from the FINAL group files. FB.1: 'needs F0: new workspace crate embed/ (package glia-embed, publish = false) with `[features] fastembed = ["dep:fastembed"]`, `fastembed = { version = "=4.9.1", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["ort-download-binaries", "hf-hub-rustls-tls"] }` (pins ort 2.0.0-rc.9, Engram's measured runtime; rustls so no system OpenSSL enters the manylinux wheel); engine `glia-embed = { path = "../embed" }` (no features) plus an engine feature `sem-eval = ["glia-embed/fastembed"]` (off by default; scripts/embedding-gate.sh and the rank gate build rank_eval with `--features sem-eval`) - never a fastembed dev-dependency'. FB.5c: 'py/Cargo.toml `[features] embed = ["glia-embed/fastembed"]`'. Seed §B: 'Its own crate behind a Cargo feature (the CLI on; whether the PyPI wheel ships it is measured in the spec run)'. FA.16: 'the crate skeleton build-domain/ (Cargo.toml with glia-core / glia-activation / glia-store / serde / serde_json, src/lib.rs doc-only slot), its workspace member line, Cargo.lock, and a HASHED_ROOTS entry in stamp/build.rs (build-domain shapes targets.gmap; parsers/build/bazel is already under the hashed `parsers` root)'. FA.17: 'the crate skeleton parsers/build/bazel/ (Cargo.toml depending on glia-core and glia-build-domain, src/lib.rs slot)'. FA.15: 'snapshots/Cargo.toml dependencies on glia-build-domain and serde_json'. FA.18: 'engine/Cargo.toml dependencies on glia-build-domain and glia-parser-bazel'. FC.17a moved its gh JSON parsing to code-domain precisely so snapshots needs no new edge for it; FA.15's serde_json edge is the one snapshots gains (serde_json is already in Cargo.lock: engine, cli use it, so no new package). VERIFIED in the local registry: fastembed 4.9.1 is Apache-2.0, pins ort / ort-sys =2.0.0-rc.9, and has features ort-download-binaries and hf-hub-rustls-tls; its non-optional dependencies include anyhow, image 0.25, ndarray 0.16, rayon, serde_json and tokenizers 0.21 with `onig` (a C build of oniguruma, BSD-2): all permissive, but heavy - which is why every edge into a crate glia-py or the engine's tests build is optional. ONE dependency commit (the 0.5.2 D0.2 / 0.5.1 C0 precedent): every Cargo.lock move of the release is here.

packets.implementation: 1. Write the three crate skeletons (Cargo.toml + doc-only src/lib.rs; the docs name the owner packets and what the crate must never do: glia-embed is never a build input and never hashed; glia-build-domain knows nothing of code; glia-parser-bazel reads `bazel query` rows only, never runs bazel - snapshots does). 2. The manifest edges in entry_points, exactly; no `[dev-dependencies]` edge on fastembed anywhere. 3. stamp/build.rs: append "build-domain" to HASHED_ROOTS (MIN_INPUTS unaffected). 4. `cargo generate-lockfile` is NOT used (it would move every locked package): `cargo build -p glia-embed --features fastembed` then `cargo build --workspace` let cargo add only the new packages; `bash scripts/check-engram-export.sh --update-lock` moves engram-export's lock the same way. 5. Licence check (a committed-nowhere python one-off whose output goes in the commit body): `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features` vs the HEAD lock's package set: every ADDED package's `license` must be within {MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, Unicode-DFS-2016, CC0-1.0, BSL-1.0, MPL-2.0} (SPDX OR / AND expressions: each OR alternative suffices, each AND term must be in the set); print `[deps] added=<n> licences=<sorted set> outside=<list|none>`; any outside -> stop and report (James decides). 6. Tree-size check, printed in the commit body: `cargo tree -p glia-py -e normal --prefix none | grep -cE '^(fastembed|ort|ort-sys|tokenizers|image|hf-hub) '` = 0 (lean wheel unless the feature is on), the same for glia-engine = 0, and > 0 for `-p glia-cli` and `-p glia-py --features embed`.
packets.acceptance: PRE-FIX: `cargo pkgid glia-embed glia-build-domain glia-parser-bazel` fails for each (HEAD). AFTER: (1) each prints a path ending `@0.5.3` (or the workspace version at the base); `git diff Cargo.lock | grep -c '^-version'` = 0 (no locked package moved, only additions). (2) `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo build -p glia-cli --no-default-features` succeed with 0 warnings; `cargo test -p glia-engine --test api_stability --test byte_identical` and `cargo test -p glia-py` green WITHOUT downloading ORT (check: `ls target/*/build | grep -c ort-sys` unchanged by those two commands from a clean `cargo clean -p ort-sys`). (3) The `[deps]` line in the commit body shows `outside=none`; the four tree-size counts are as in step 6. (4) `grep -c 'build-domain' stamp/build.rs` = 1 and `cargo build -p glia-stamp` passes its MIN_INPUTS floor. (5) `bash scripts/check-engram-export.sh` ends `[engram-export] check: ok`. (6) the three lib.rs files hold only `//!` lines; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

packets.title: Measured experiment (S4): the declaration-surface fingerprint and a commit-replay harness that sizes the body-only fast path per language; its report fixes which languages get a fast-path packet and in what order
packets.area: FA - incremental resolution (A: Stack Graphs-style partial paths + watch A2)
packets.rationale: Section A's Stack Graphs bet is 'one partial-path model across 20 languages is the unknown' (0.5.1 plan section 5), and R2-watch section 12 spike S4 is the open sizing question: 'replay the last ~200 commits ... count the share whose declaration surface is unchanged. Sizes A2's payoff.' R2-watch section 13 names single-language repos (one big group: glia's Rust, grpc-go's Go) as where only A2 helps. The task asks to start with the languages where it pays and justify the order, so this packet measures before any builder is touched. The model this release adopts (stated in the report, not literal github/stack-graphs, which is archived and would replace every builder with a per-language TSG DSL): per file a PARTIAL = its SURFACE (declarations: node ids / kinds / qnames / nav parents, imports with their rows, heritage refs, field / return types, method signatures, properties, the surface NavFacts) plus its BODY stubs (call sites, non-heritage refs, local types, body NavFacts, node cells); STITCHING = the builder's per-file resolution of the body stubs against the group's surface index (SymbolTable plus the language index: RustIndex, GoPackages, ...). A body-only edit leaves every other file's stitching valid.
entry_points: engine/src/cache.rs - `pub fn surface_fingerprint(fp: &FileParse) -> Option<u64>` beside the pub(crate) `parse_fingerprint`: xxh64 over a canonical serialization of the surface only (CanonicalNav-style ordered maps); `pub fn surface_class(f: &NavFact) -> Part` (Part::Surface | Part::Body), an EXHAUSTIVE match over every NavFact variant (no wildcard: NavFact is not #[non_exhaustive], so a new variant fails to compile until it is classified); `pub fn surface_language(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str>` (the engine's language detection, for the example); reached as `glia_engine::cache::surface_fingerprint` (engine::cache is a `pub mod`)
engine/examples/surface_replay.rs (new) - `cargo run --release -p glia-engine --example surface_replay -- --repo <path> --commits 200 [--rev <tip>] --out <json>`
dev-notes/surface-replay-0.5.4.md (new) - the report: per (repo, language) the body-only share, the group build ms, the projected saving, PASS / FAIL per language and the resulting packet order
packets.implementation:
1. engine/src/cache.rs: `pub enum Part { Surface, Body }` and `pub fn surface_class(f: &NavFact) -> Part`. Classification rule: a fact is Surface when ANOTHER file's resolution may read it (a builder or language hook looks it up by name across files), Body when only its own scope's resolution reads it. Read each variant's reader before classifying (grep the variant name in graph/src). Expected from the variant docs in code-domain/src/lib.rs (verify each): Surface - DeclaresFn, UsingNamespace, UsingName, FieldMount, InternalLinkage, ValueLiteral (read by const folds across files), AbstractMethod, UrlPrefixKey, TypeAlias, GoStringConst, GoPackageName, SliceResult, ReExportStar, ReExportNamespace, ReExportName, ExportLocal, Exports, EvmAbi, RiverpodProvider, Getter, Setter (`Const` / `Param` / `Field` are variants of the nested `Mount` enum MountArg / FieldMount carry, not NavFact variants: the match has the 27 NavFact arms); Body - MountArg (Go mounts re-key ROUTEs through RESOLVED calls: also flag it as a cross-file body dependency, below), ClientHost, ClientBase, MemberRead, MemberWrite, ReceiverType. Doc each arm in one line. 2. `surface_fingerprint(fp)`: serialize, in this order, through the same HashWriter / bincode streaming parse_fingerprint uses: (a) nodes as (id, kind, qname) sorted by id - NOT their cells (POSITION / CODE move on any edit); (b) nav.name_by_id, qname_by_id, kind_by_id, parent_of, children_of, field_types, return_types, method_sigs (by_id / by_name ordered, exactly as CanonicalNav does), and the local_types entries of MODULE scopes only (module-level / package-level variables: an importer's or another package file's receiver typing reads them, e.g. Go package vars through GoPackages, a Python module-level `x = Foo()` imported by name), in every language; (c) properties sorted; (d) imports with their rows (an IMPORTS edge's EVIDENCE line is the import row, so a moved import is a surface change); (e) refs whose category is INHERITS_FROM or IMPLEMENTS (heritage: resolution follows heritage edges), with rows; (f) nav_facts restricted to surface_class == Surface, per scope in id order, each scope's list in parser order. `None` when serialization fails. Also `pub fn surface_fingerprint_strict(fp)` = the same plus every node's POSITION cell payload (the declaration rows): the report measures both, because a fast path that cannot re-derive line-carrying outputs would need the strict one. 3. engine/examples/surface_replay.rs: args --repo, --commits N (default 200), --rev (default HEAD), --out. For each of the last N first-parent commits (`git rev-list --first-parent -n N `; std::process::Command in an example only, never in a build), for each modified (not added / deleted / renamed: `git diff --name-status ^ `, status M) file with a source language (`glia_engine::cache::surface_language`, a new pub fn in cache.rs delegating to the pub(crate) `crate::extract::detect_language`, which an example cannot call), read both blobs (`git show ^:

` / `:

`), parse each with `glia_engine::parse_one` (the flat extract API), compute surface_fingerprint and surface_fingerprint_strict, and record (commit, path, lang, loose_equal, strict_equal, has_body_cross_dep) where has_body_cross_dep = the file's parse holds a Body fact some OTHER file's resolution reads (MountArg today). Then time what a watch update spends on the group, through the public watch API (no hand-assembled builder inputs: build_rust needs the Cargo crates, the TS family its alias resolver): on a `git archive` copy of the repo at --rev in a temp dir, `glia_engine::watch::WatchSession::open`, then per language with edits 3 updates, each appending (then, next update, removing) one comment line in a file of that language (a body-only touch that rebuilds exactly its group); from each WatchUpdate whose `groups_rebuilt` is exactly that group, record phase_ms.language_build (group_ms), phase_ms.clone (clone_ms) and phase_ms.total (update_ms); medians of 3. Run with GLIA_THREADS=1 so group_ms is one group's sequential cost. 4. CONTROLS, run in the same replay: (i) null control: per commit up to 20 unmodified source files (same blob at ^ and ) are parsed twice and fingerprinted; any inequality is a fingerprint-stability failure and the whole run fails (no verdict is printed until it is fixed); (ii) positive control: every modified file whose diff adds or removes a line matching the language's top-level declaration pattern (def / class / fn / func / function / interface / struct / impl / trait / type at the file's top indent) must come out surface-changed; each violation is listed in the report and either explained (the declaration is nested in a body, so it IS body) or fixed in surface_class / surface_fingerprint before any verdict. 5a. Per (repo, language): edits, body_only_loose = share with loose_equal && !has_body_cross_dep, body_only_strict, group_ms, update_ms, build_share = group_ms / update_ms, projected_saving_ms = body_only_loose x group_ms (an UPPER bound: the fast path still stitches the edited files and re-fills the group's evidence). Print one `[surface-replay] repo= lang= edits= body_only=/ group_ms= update_ms= build_share= clone_ms= saving_ms= controls= verdict=` line per row and write --out JSON (rows sorted by repo, lang). 5. PASS RULE (stated in the report before the numbers): a language PASSES when, on at least one measured repo, edits >= 30, body_only_loose >= 0.40, group_ms >= 250 (release build), build_share >= 0.25 (the group build is a quarter of the update, so cutting it is visible end to end), and both controls hold. FA.24's rule (the clone cut) is read off the same rows: clone_ms >= 50 and clone_ms >= 0.20 x update_ms on at least one measured repo. Repos (public, with history; never ~/Code/webplatform, never a private repo): glia at its v0.5.2 tag (Rust), pop-os/shell (~/Code/shell, TypeScript), gorilla/websocket (~/Code/websocket, Go), and pallets/flask cloned fresh with full history into the scratchpad (Python; no local public Python repo has history). grpc-go at ~/Code/grpc-go is shallow (1 commit): `git fetch --unshallow` it if the network allows and add its row, else say so in the report. 6. dev-notes/surface-replay-0.5.4.md: the model (rationale's paragraph), the pass rules (fast path and FA.24's clone rule), the controls' results, the table (every row, both fingerprints), the verdicts and the ORDER of the language packets that pass: by projected_saving_ms descending, ties by language name. FA.3 (Python, the reference implementation of the per-file stitching seam) is built when Python passes OR any other language passes (it carries the seam the others reuse); FA.5 Rust, FA.6 TypeScript family and FA.7 Go each only on their own PASS. Aggregate numbers only (public repos). FA.24 (copy-free reuse of unchanged groups) is built only on its own clone rule's PASS.
packets.acceptance: `cargo build --release -p glia-engine --example surface_replay` builds; `cargo test -p glia-engine --lib cache::` green with new tests: (a) a body-only edit of a Python and a Rust fixture file (a statement inside a fn body changed, lines below shifted) keeps surface_fingerprint equal and changes surface_fingerprint_strict and parse_fingerprint; (b) adding a fn, renaming a class, changing an import or a base class changes surface_fingerprint; (c) the fingerprint is equal for two parses of one source made in different hash-map fill orders (parse twice in one process with a different insertion order forced through a test helper, as parse_fingerprint's tests do). `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. (d) a module-level variable's type change (`x = Foo()` -> `x = Bar()` at module scope) changes surface_fingerprint; a local's inside a fn does not. `cargo run --release -p glia-engine --example surface_replay -- --repo <glia v0.5.2 archive> --commits 200 --out <json>` runs to completion with `controls=ok` on every row. The report exists with one row per (repo, language) measured, both fingerprints, both controls' results, an explicit PASS / FAIL per language under the stated rule, and FA.24's clone verdict.

packets.title: Canonical per-graph order: every RepoGraph's intra edges sorted by glia_core::canonical_edge_cmp and its unresolved_calls / unresolved_refs by a total key at the end of each group build (before the evidence fill), so a graph built in any emission order has one byte form
packets.area: FA - incremental resolution (A: Stack Graphs-style partial paths + watch A2)
packets.rationale: R2-watch section 5, A2 need (a): 'canonical intra-edge order in RepoGraph (today intra edges are emission-ordered; only cross edges get canonical_edge_cmp, merged.rs)'. A fast path that re-resolves one file's body appends that file's edges after everyone else's, so without a canonical order its graph could never be byte-identical to a clean build. MergedGraph::sort_cross_edges is the precedent (graph/src/merged.rs). unresolved_calls / unresolved_refs are persisted in the code section (store/src/code_section.rs `unresolved_calls` / `unresolved_refs`), so they need a total order too. A one-time content change of every shard's bytes, declared.
entry_points: graph/src/types.rs - `impl RepoGraph { pub fn canonicalize(&mut self) }`: edges.sort_unstable_by(canonical_edge_cmp); unresolved_calls sorted by (from.0, line, qualifier_key); unresolved_refs by (from.0, from_module.0, category.0, line, qualifier_key), qualifier_key a (variant index, strings) tuple

engine/src/build/lang_build.rs - build_one: `g.canonicalize()` right after `stamp_graph_edges` and before `HeritageTally::of` / `LineTally` / `fill_group_evidence` (GroupFill indexes edges by position, so the sort must precede it)
engine/src/build/mod.rs - aux_graphs: the region / project / docs graphs canonicalized too (they are shards)
packets.implementation:
1. graph/src/types.rs: RepoGraph::canonicalize as in entry_points. qualifier_key(&CallQualifier) -> (u8, &str, &str): Bare(n) -> (0, n, ""), SelfMethod(n) -> (1, n, ""), SuperMethod(n) -> (2, n, ""), Attribute{base,name} -> (3, base, name), ComplexReceiver{receiver,name} -> (4, receiver, name) (an exhaustive match). Stable sorts for the unresolved lists (equal keys keep parser order, which is per-file deterministic). Doc: why (a fast path splices one file's edges; a clean build must not depend on emission order) and that every builder still emits in its own order.
2. engine/src/build/lang_build.rs build_one: insert the call as in entry_points. engine/src/build/mod.rs aux_graphs: canonicalize each graph it pushes.
3. Check every reader that depended on intra-edge order: grep in engine/src and graph/src for loops over `g.edges` / `graph.edges` that pick a FIRST match (`.find(`, `.position(`, a `break` after a hit, `first`), in passes run after the group build (CODE_PASSES in engine/src/profile.rs, persist, delta). For each, either confirm the choice is order-free (it scans all and picks by a total key) or make it so in this packet (pick by (qname, kind) as DE.1 does). List each site checked in the commit body.
4. Proof that only ORDER moved (a `#[cfg(test)]` switch in glia-graph is invisible to an engine integration test, so the reference is captured from the unchanged tree): STEP 0, before any other edit, add the new test fn to engine/tests/build_parity.rs and run it with GLIA_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 on the parent tree: it builds the fixture corpus (the repos the file already uses) and writes, per fixture, engine/tests/data/canonical/<fixture>.multiset.txt: per graph the sorted multiset of (from qname, to qname, category, confidence, cells), the sorted node list and the sorted unresolved lists. packets.implementation:
Model (doc it at the top of partial.rs): a file's PARTIAL is its surface plus its body stubs (FA.1's surface_class); the group's SURFACE INDEX is RepoGraph.symbols + nav's declaration maps; STITCHING resolves body stubs against it. A body-only edit = every edited file's engine::cache::surface_fingerprint is unchanged (the engine checks this before calling; the graph crate cannot see the engine, so rebuild_* re-checks the cheap invariant itself: the edit's node id set, kinds and qnames equal the graph's nodes owned by that file, else Refused::SurfaceMoved(path)).
1. File ownership: a node belongs to the file whose MODULE is its nav ancestor (walk parent_of to the MODULE; Python MODULE qname is the file's). `file_nodes(g, module_id) -> BTreeSet<NodeId>`.
2. Split build_python with NO behaviour change for a clean build: python_surface = merge_parses + build_symbol_table + the BINDING half of resolve_imports_python (what it writes into SymbolTable.module_import_bindings and the same-stem picks); python_stitch(files) = for the given files, in parse order: the IMPORTS-edge half of resolve_imports_python for their imports, resolve_calls over their calls, resolve_refs over their refs, emit_method_level_implements restricted to their classes. A clean build_python = surface then stitch(all files). If resolve_imports_python cannot be split without changing which bindings exist (a binding that depends on edges emitted earlier), keep it whole in the surface and note it; IMPORTS edges then carry rows that are in the surface fingerprint anyway (FA.1 step 2d). The evidence tally (`[evidence-graph]`) is summed over the stitch calls.
3. rebuild_python_bodies(g, edits): for each edit (sorted by its MODULE qname): (a) owned = file_nodes; (b) drop_file_outputs: remove every edge whose `from` is in owned, every unresolved_calls entry whose `from` is in owned, every unresolved_refs entry whose `from_module` is the file's MODULE; (c) replace each owned node's cells with the edit parse's node cells (same ids by the surface check), and the file's parse edges (fp.edges) are pushed again; (d) replace_file_nav: local_types and nav_facts entries of the owned scopes with the parse's; (e) python_stitch(g, the edit's imports / calls / refs / classes); then g.canonicalize() (FA.2). Duplicate-NodeId cells (merge_parses appends cells when two parses declare one id) are a Refused::Unsupported("shared node") case: detect them (an owned node whose id appears in another file's nav) and refuse.
4. Nothing else in g may depend on the edited file's body: Python's builder reads no body fact across files (verify by reading resolve_calls' receiver path: it reads the CALLER's own local_types and field_types / return_types, which are surface). Document the verification in partial.rs.
5. Unit tests in partial.rs (cfg(test), fixtures as inline parses through glia_parser_python's parse fn, which glia-graph has as a dev-dependency): for 6 edits (a call added, a call removed, a call moved down 3 lines, a body line inserted above two defs, a decorator-free method body change, an edit in a file that others import) assert `rebuild_python_bodies(build_python(old_parses), edits)` == `build_python(new_parses)` after canonicalize, compared field by field (nodes, edges, unresolved lists, properties; nav maps compared as sorted vecs); and a surface change (a def added) returns Refused::SurfaceMoved.

packets.title: Multi-repo WatchSession: `WatchSession::open_many(roots, opts)` builds the repos exactly as generate_many does (one walk per repo, identities disambiguated, the proto service set unioned, one joint pass tail) and `apply` routes each changed path to the repo whose root holds it
packets.area: FA - multi-repo watch (A: glia watch --with)
packets.rationale: 0.5.2 plan Q13 / section 3: multi-repo `glia watch --with` is 0.5.4's. R2-watch question 3: 'The proto service set is build-wide (mod.rs), so it touches every repo.' engine/src/build/mod.rs `assemble_many_with` is the composition to reproduce: phase 1 walks every repo and unions the RpcContext, disambiguates identities (`disambiguate`), phase 2 builds each against the union; `finish_build` runs the passes once over all graphs in argument order. Every update's graph must equal a clean generate_many of the same trees.
entry_points: engine/src/watch.rs - `pub fn open_many(roots: &[String], opts: &BuildOptions) -> Result<WatchSession, String>` (open(root) becomes open_many(&[root])); `pub fn roots(&self) -> Vec<&str>`
engine/src/build/mod.rs - `disambiguate` and `canonical_display` become pub(crate) for the session (no logic change)
packets.implementation:
1. open_many: for each root (argument order): plan_walk + read_walk (with stat stamps) as open does, repo_identity; then disambiguate the identities against each other with assemble_many_with's rule (canonical_display of each root); one RpcContext from every repo's files (rpc.add_files in argument order); Setup per repo (overlay text: never - the session reads each root's own .glia/overlay.toml, as a multi-repo build does for slots > 0; slot 0 too since watch has no overlay_text); build: per repo the DC.2 stages (parse_and_graft with the repo's cache and the SHARED rpc, plan / fingerprint / reuse / build / fold groups, repo_markers, aux_graphs) appended in argument order, fills aligned, then ONE finish_build(graphs, fills, inputs (one RepoInputs per repo, argument order), opts, repos.len(), started); GenerateResult.repo_labels = arch::repo_label_map over (RepoId, root) pairs, repo_roots first-wins, parse_errors concatenated in argument order - exactly assemble_many_with's.
2. A root that is not a directory: Err (unlike generate_many, which keeps going: a watch needs every repo; doc it). Nested roots (one root inside another, after canonicalisation) are refused: Err `nested watch roots: <inner> is inside <outer>` - a clean generate_many reads the inner repo's files in BOTH walks, which a path router cannot reproduce. `save_cache` saves every repo's ParseCache to its own root (single repo: unchanged), so the CLI and pyo3 persist every cache through it.
3. apply(changed): each path goes to the one repo whose abs_roots hold it (roots never nest: step 2); paths under no root count `outside`. Each repo with named paths re-reads / re-plans as today (High durability is per repo). Then: services_fp = fp of the union over every repo's files; a union change is a full_rebuild reason `proto_services` for every repo's groups (their fingerprints include it). Repos with no named path are not re-read, but parse_and_graft still runs for every repo (their ParseCache entries, DC.4 memos and cached group builds make an untouched repo a cache hit throughout), so the joint graph is assembled from fresh stage outputs in argument order, exactly as a clean generate_many composes them. Scoped delta: the scope sides are the union of each repo's rebuilt groups' graph indexes offset by the repo's first graph index in the joint result.
4. Identity: a High `identity` path in one repo re-reads its identity and re-runs disambiguate over all repos; if any RepoId changed, every repo's cache context is revalidated (validate_context clears it) and the update is a full_rebuild `identity`.
5. EA.7's RankCache: built from the joint result's repo_roots / repo_labels, replaced after a changed update as today.
6. Markers: `[watch] open repos=<n> repo=<label1,label2,..> files=<n> groups=<g> nodes=<N> edges=<E> took=<ms>` (open of one repo keeps its old text: `repos=` is printed only when n > 1); the update line's `repo=` lists the repos that had named paths.
7. Unit tests in watch.rs (temp dirs): open_many over two tiny repos equals generate_many_opts of the same roots node-for-node (persisted bytes); a path in repo 2 rebuilds only repo 2's groups (`groups_rebuilt` keys carry the repo label prefix `<label>:<key>` when n > 1 - doc it); open_many over nested roots is an Err naming both; save_cache writes each repo's parse_cache.bin.

packets.rationale: The single-repo DC.10a / DC.10b gates (engine/tests/watch_parity.rs) are why watch is trusted; open_many (FA.9) needs the same bar, with the cross-repo inputs a single repo never exercises: the unioned proto service set (a .proto edited in the server repo moves the client repo's RPC needles), cross-repo resolvers (HTTP_CALLS between repos), SAME_AS identity across repos and a High input in one repo only.

packets.implementation:
1. Fixture: repo A (server): `proto/greeter.proto` (service Greeter, rpc Hi), a Go server implementing it, a Go HTTP handler `GET /api/orders`, `go.mod` module `example.com/server`; repo B (client): a Go gRPC client calling GreeterClient.Hi, a TS fetch of `/api/orders`, and a `go.mod` requiring `example.com/server`, so the manifest_name / package_name identity classes form across repos.
2. After open_many([A, B]) and after every update: persist the session's layout to a temp dir and compare its bytes (every file) with `generate_many_opts([A, B], false, &opts)` + persist_result to another temp dir; also compare GenerateResult.parse_errors. Use the helper watch_parity.rs uses for single repos (layout byte comparison).
3. Scripted sequences: (a) body edit in B's client; (b) add an rpc to the .proto in A (B's needles must move: full_rebuild `proto_services`); (c) edit A's HTTP route path (cross-repo HTTP_CALLS edge removed / re-added); (d) edit B's go.mod require (High in B only); (e) add then delete a file in A; (f) a two-repo update (paths in both); (g) an .glia/overlay.toml added to B.
4. Random: 3 seeds x 15 ops over the op table {body edit A/B, decl edit A/B, add / remove file A/B, proto edit, go.mod touch, noop touch}, each op's expected group set computed by an oracle like watch_parity's `group_of`; assert byte identity after each op and that groups_rebuilt is a superset of the oracle's set.
5. Mark the slow random test #[ignore] only if it exceeds 60 s debug; otherwise it runs in the default suite.

packets.title: One memory budget, watch half: `engine::memory::MemoryBudget` (GLIA_MEMORY_BUDGET_MB / an explicit value), per-update RSS accounting in WatchSession, LRU eviction of cached group builds and build memos past the budget, a `[watch] rss` marker, `--memory-budget-mb` / `memory_budget_mb=`, and a release RSS gate
packets.area: FA - memory budget (F item 3: watch + rules)
packets.rationale: Section F item 3 (James 2026-10-16: 'yep add it'): 'Measure RSS over repeated applies on the 0.5.2 WatchSession, then cap or evict, with a [watch] RSS marker and a gate.' Data: it levels off (100 updates on glia: first 562 MB, plateau 615-685 MB, debug); repo-graph-8d measured a held session at 940 MB vs 500 MB for a rebuild loop on glia. 'The budget question is the plateau's size, not a leak.' What a session holds beyond one graph (R2-watch section 13: about 3x one graph): every group's cached pre-pass LangBuild (CachedGroup, engine/src/watch.rs), the ParseCache entries and DC.4 BuildMemo (engine/src/build/memo.rs), the result. The cached groups and memos are pure caches (a hit replays exactly what a miss computes), so evicting them changes time, never bytes. ALREADY SHIPPED, not respecced: memo entries of paths no longer walked are dropped (BuildMemo::retain, DC.4) and the CLI prints the RSS series (`[watch] emitted ... rss_mb=`, DC.8).

packets.title: OrgPackageResolver (`resolver:org_packages`, after identity): an importer's IMPORT_BINDINGS row whose package is the SAME_AS manifest_name class of a sibling PROJECT routes to that project's entry MODULE (IMPORTS, DERIVED) - npm and Go first
packets.area: FA - org-internal package routing (A: on SAME_AS)
packets.rationale: Section A, on 0.5.2's SAME_AS: IdentityResolver's `manifest_name` rule (graph/src/resolvers/identity.rs, FACT) already joins a manifest-labelled PROJECT and the PACKAGE_DEPs naming it (same_as::project_dep_key / dep_identity_key), across repos and inside a monorepo. That class says 'this dependency IS that sibling project'; routing the import statements through it gives the IMPORTS edge between the two codebases. A new resolver per CLAUDE.md 'Adding a New Cross-Graph Resolver': graph/src/resolvers/org_packages.rs, two lines in resolvers/mod.rs, one PassSpec in engine/src/profile.rs with `after: ["identity"]` (it reads SAME_AS edges, so it must run after the identity pass).
entry_points: graph/src/resolvers/org_packages.rs (new) - `pub struct OrgPackageResolver;` (unit struct) implementing CrossGraphResolver; `struct PackageIndex` (per manifest_name class: the PROJECT node, its ecosystem, its root dir from the PROJECT's ORIGIN cell, the importer-side spec prefix)
graph/src/resolvers/mod.rs - `mod org_packages;` + `pub use org_packages::OrgPackageResolver;`

engine/src/profile.rs - a Resolve PassSpec `org_packages` after `identity` (the 18th Resolve pass), populates [] (edges only); the `code_passes_order_is_head_order` / `populates_is_exact` pins and the `[passes] domain=code resolve=18 post=9 finalize=2` expectation updated
packets.implementation:
1. Read SAME_AS cross edges whose EVIDENCE rule is `manifest_name` (or `manifest_name/diverged`): group by center; each class has one PROJECT and >= 1 PACKAGE_DEP. Index per class: ecosystem from the dep qname (`package:<eco>:<name>`), the PROJECT's root path (its ORIGIN `project_root` cell: path field; read the cell shape in engine/src/walk.rs / the project graph builder), its repo (graph index).
2. Importer side: every MODULE with an IMPORT_BINDINGS cell (FA.21) in a graph whose repo holds a PACKAGE_DEP member of the class (the dependency must be DECLARED by the importer's repo - the FACT the SAME_AS class rests on); a row matches the class when: npm - spec == name or starts with `name/`; gomod - spec == module path or starts with `modpath/`.
3. Target module: npm - spec == name: the project's entry MODULE: in order `<root>/index`, `<root>/src/index` (TS / JS module qnames: read resolve_ts_source's qname shape in engine/src/build/lang_build.rs `ts_path_qname`), the package.json `main` / `module` / `types` are NOT read here (no manifest text in the graph: note it); spec `name/sub/path` -> `<root>/sub/path` then `<root>/src/sub/path` (file or `::index`). go - `modpath/sub` -> the Go package directory `<root>/sub`, whose file MODULEs carry file-path qnames: the edge targets exactly what resolve_imports_go (graph/src/imports.rs) targets for an in-repo import of a package directory (read its in-repo rule and mirror it: same target node choice, one edge per imported package).
4. Emit cross edge IMPORTS importer MODULE -> target MODULE, Confidence::Medium (DERIVED: two FACT links joined by a rule), EVIDENCE emitter `resolver:org_packages`, rule `org_import`, file = the importer's POSITION file, line = the row's line. No edge when the importer MODULE already has an IMPORTS edge to that target (an in-repo binding the language build made, e.g. a monorepo whose tsconfig paths or Cargo workspace bind the package): org routing only fills what the build left unbound. A row matching two classes (nested package names) takes the longest name; a row whose target module is absent emits nothing and counts `unrouted`.
5. engine/tests/org_packages.rs: generate_many over two temp repos - app (package.json depends on `@acme/lib`; `import { greet } from '@acme/lib'`; a Go file importing `example.com/acme/lib/text`) and lib (package.json name `@acme/lib` with src/index.ts exporting greet; go.mod `module example.com/acme/lib` with text/text.go) - expect the two IMPORTS cross edges with rule org_import; a monorepo variant (both under one repo, npm workspaces) routes too; an app WITHOUT the dependency declared routes nothing (forbid); a layout merge of the two single-repo layouts (merge::merge_layouts) yields the same cross edges (merge == joint build).

packets.title: Org routing, calls and the other ecosystems: unresolved call sites and refs whose name or base an IMPORT_BINDINGS row binds are bound to the sibling's exported declaration (CALLS / USES, DERIVED), and cargo / pypi classes route (crate root, top-level packages)
packets.area: FA - org-internal package routing (A: on SAME_AS)
packets.rationale: An IMPORTS edge between the two codebases is the first half; the value is the call-level link (blast radius of `greet` reaches `run` in the app repo). The importer's call sites that named the external binding stayed unresolved and are persisted (RepoGraph.unresolved_calls: CallSite { from, qualifier, line }; unresolved_refs). Cargo and PyPI are the other two ecosystems same_as::project_dep_key maps (npm, gomod, cargo, pypi, composer).
entry_points: graph/src/resolvers/org_packages.rs - `fn bind_calls(merged, routes) -> Vec<Edge>`: per importer MODULE, its routed rows' local names -> target scope (a MODULE or a declaration); every unresolved CallSite whose caller's MODULE is that importer: Bare(alias) -> the target module's top-level declaration named `name` (Symbol import) ; Attribute{base: alias, name: f} -> the target module's (or Go package dir's) top-level declaration `f` (Module import / namespace import); emits CALLS, Medium, rule `org_call`; unresolved_refs of USES / INJECTS / HANDLED_BY categories the same way, rule `org_ref`

graph/src/resolvers/org_packages.rs - cargo: `name::path::item` -> the crate root MODULE (`<root>/src/lib` qname per rust_paths' crate-root rule) and the path's modules; pypi: `pkg.mod` -> `<root>/pkg/mod` or `<root>/src/pkg/mod` MODULE
packets.implementation:
1. A declaration lookup reads persisted structure only (merge == joint build): a target module's top-level declarations = its nav children (children_of / name_by_id in RepoGraph.nav, persisted in CodeNavStore - verify which nav maps the store keeps; if children_of is not persisted, use parent_of inverted). For a TS barrel target, follow the module's IMPORTS edges with EVIDENCE rule `reexport` (DT.1q, persisted edges) one level at a time, depth <= 8, and take a uniquely named exported declaration; two candidates -> no edge (`ambiguous`).
2. The caller's MODULE: walk the caller's nav parent chain to its MODULE (the same walk calls.rs uses). Only call sites still in unresolved_calls are considered: a site the language build bound is never re-bound.
3. Cargo: rows from IMPORT_BINDINGS for Rust (`use org_lib::util::helper` -> spec `org_lib::util`, name `helper`): the crate name normalised `-` -> `_` matches same_as's cargo key; target = the crate's `src/lib.rs` MODULE then each path segment as a child module (`util` -> `<root>/src/util` or `<root>/src/util/mod`). PyPI: the importer's top-level module name equals the distribution name normalised (`my-lib` -> `my_lib`) or a top-level package dir under the project root (`<root>/<pkg>` or `<root>/src/<pkg>`); a distribution whose import name differs and no dir matches routes nothing (counted).
4. Tests (engine/tests/org_packages.rs): the TS call `greet('x')` (Bare via a named import, and `lib.greet()` via a namespace import), the Go `text.Upper()`, a Rust `helper()` through `use org_lib::util::helper`, a Python `helper()` through `from org_lib.util import helper`, a barrel re-export (lib/src/index.ts `export * from './greet'`), an ambiguous barrel -> no edge, merge == joint build for the CALLS edges, blast_radius on lib's greet reaches app's run (the answer walks the new cross edge), and a one-repo Cargo workspace of two crates with a path dependency (glia's own shape) gains NO org_* edge (its `use` sites are bound by the Rust build through rust_crates, so none is left unresolved).

packets.title: Watch reuses an unchanged group's post-pass graph by move instead of deep-cloning its cached pre-pass build (0.5.2 W7 DC.7b, the A2 follow-on), only if FA.1's clone rule passes
packets.area: FA - incremental resolution (A: Stack Graphs-style partial paths + watch A2)
packets.rationale: 0.5.2 W7 (DC.7b) left a section E item tied to A2: 'a watch update deep-clones every group (50-221 ms on glia) by design; cutting it needs passes that do not mutate group graphs (section A, A2)'. A layout merge already proves the needed property: merge.rs re-runs every resolver and pass over graphs a previous build's passes already ran on, after MergedGraph::undo_pass_mutations (LC.10a) and dropping resolver:* / pass:* cross edges, and merge == joint build is tested. So an unchanged group's graph can be taken from the previous update's result by move and prepared the way a merge prepares a member, with no deep clone in or out. The draft kept the clone with no packet; under 'no deferrals' it gets a gated packet: FA.1 measures clone_ms per repo and this is built only if the clone is a real share of an update.

packets.title: glia-embed: the Embedder trait, the deterministic test-only HashEmbedder, the fastembed BGESmallENV15 adapter (feature `fastembed`), the f32 little-endian codec and cosine, with a CPU bit-identity test
packets.area: FB embeddings: the embedder crate
packets.rationale: next-leap-0.5.4.md §B: glia embeds itself with fastembed-rs / bge-small (James 2026-10-16, 'shouldn't we bring parts of engram in'), copying no Engram code; §3 ruling 3: glia's half first against fixtures with 'a deterministic test-only embedding'. Engram's measured learnings bind: `EmbeddingModel::BGESmallENV15` = Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5 onnx/model.onnx fp32, 384 dims, CLS pooling, ort 2.0.0-rc.9 (fastembed 4.9.1 resolves exactly that, ~/.cargo/registry fastembed-4.9.1 src/models/text_embedding.rs: model_code Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5, model_file onnx/model.onnx, dim 384); not BGESmallENV15Q; L2-normalised output, rank by raw cosine; FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR defaults to `.fastembed_cache` under the CWD (fastembed-4.9.1 src/common.rs) so glia must set a user cache, never a repo dir; two ORT sessions at once thrash and fastembed 4.9.1 sets intra-op threads = available_parallelism with no knob (src/text_embedding/impl.rs try_new), so glia holds ONE session and feeds sequential 256-text chunks (one `embed(chunk, Some(256))` call per chunk: par_chunks then yields one chunk, no concurrent session runs). A separate crate keeps ONNX out of the engine's normal tree: the engine needs only the trait (the query is embedded by the caller's embedder, FB.4 / FB.7a).

embed/src/lib.rs - `pub struct HashEmbedder` (model `glia-test-hash-v1/64`, 64 dims), `pub fn named(name: &str) -> Result<Box<dyn Embedder>, String>` (`test-hash` always; `bge-small` only with feature `fastembed`)
embed/src/fast.rs (new, `#[cfg(feature = "fastembed")] mod fast;`) - `pub struct FastEmbedder` over one `fastembed::TextEmbedding`
embed/src/codec.rs (new) - `to_le_bytes(&[f32]) -> Vec<u8>`, `from_le_bytes(&[u8], dims) -> Result<Vec<f32>, String>`, `l2_normalise`, `cosine` (dot of unit vectors)

packets.implementation:
Built on F0's crate skeleton (embed/Cargo.toml: package glia-embed, `[features] fastembed = ["dep:fastembed"]`, fastembed =4.9.1 optional, default-features off, features ort-download-binaries + hf-hub-rustls-tls; workspace member; engine / cli / py deps). This packet writes code only.
1. lib.rs: module doc (what the crate is, that it is never a build input, Engram's learnings as rules). `pub const MODEL_BGE_SMALL: &str = "Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5";` `pub const DIMS_BGE_SMALL: u32 = 384;` `pub const MODEL_TEST_HASH: &str = "glia-test-hash-v1/64";` `pub const CHUNK: usize = 256;` `pub const MODEL_NAMES: [&str; 2] = ["bge-small", "test-hash"];` (the CLI / py spellings). The trait as in entry_points; `embed` returns one L2-normalised vector per text in input order, every vector `dims()` long, or Err naming the failing chunk. `named(name)`: `test-hash` -> HashEmbedder; `bge-small` -> FastEmbedder::new()? under cfg(feature), else Err("glia was built without the embedding model (feature fastembed): use --model test-hash or a build with embeddings"); other -> Err listing MODEL_NAMES.
2. HashEmbedder (deterministic, test-only, documented as such: rows it writes carry its own model, so no reader of bge rows ever reads them): tokens = the text split on non-alphanumerics, then camel steps (lower->Upper, letter->digit), lowercased, tokens of 2+ chars; for each token t, h = xxh64-free FNV-1a 64 of t's bytes (inline fn, no new dependency); slot = h % 64; sign = +1 if bit 63 set else -1; v[slot] += sign; then also every adjacent token pair 't1 t2' the same way at weight 0.5 (so word order counts a little). Zero vector (no token) -> v[0] = 1.0. l2_normalise. Pure integer hashing and f32 adds in token order: bit-identical on every machine.
3. fast.rs: `FastEmbedder::new() -> Result<Self, String>`: cache dir = env FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR if set and non-empty, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/glia/fastembed`, else `$HOME/.cache/glia/fastembed` (Err when neither env is set); create it; `TextEmbedding::try_new(InitOptions::new(EmbeddingModel::BGESmallENV15).with_cache_dir(dir).with_show_download_progress(false))`; store `Mutex<TextEmbedding>` and the dir. `pub fn refuse_repo_dir(&self, repo_root: &Path) -> Result<(), String>`: Err when the canonical cache dir is under the canonical repo root (Engram's gotcha; FB.5a calls it). `embed`: for each CHUNK-sized slice, one `model.embed(slice.to_vec(), Some(CHUNK))` call, sequential, then l2_normalise each (fastembed already normalises; renormalising a unit vector is the identity up to rounding, so do it only when |norm - 1| > 1e-6, keeping bit identity with Engram's raw vectors). Marker on first load: `[embed] model load model=Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5 dims=384 cache=<dir> ms=<t>`.
4. codec.rs: little-endian f32 (the contract, engram-ask §5 'f32 little-endian agreed'); from_le_bytes Err when len != dims*4 or a value is not finite. cosine(a, b) = sum a_i*b_i in index order as f32 accumulated in f64 (deterministic order).
5. Tests: hash_embedder.rs - same text twice -> identical bytes; `UserService.getUser` vs `user service get user` -> cosine > 0.9; unrelated -> < 0.5; empty text -> unit e0; every output unit-norm within 1e-6; dims 64; named("nope") Err lists both names; without the feature named("bge-small") Err mentions --model test-hash (a cfg(not(feature)) test). fastembed_cpu.rs (#[ignore], needs the model download): the CPU determinism gate from §B - 300 mixed texts embedded alone, as one batch, and as 3 shuffled batches give bit-identical vectors per text; dims 384; unit norm; two FastEmbedder::new() in sequence (never concurrent).

packets.title: The VectorRow contract, written and validated: optional `text_hash` (`<recipe>:<16 hex>`), `model` and `dims` required for a written row, one model per sidecar, key (qname, kind); `external_inputs::audit_vectors` and `glia cell ls --check` report mixed models, missing model, dims disagreement, duplicate keys and non-finite / non-unit payloads
packets.area: FB embeddings: the sidecar contract
packets.rationale: §B 'The sidecar stays writer-agnostic: the written VectorRow contract and its validator (rows whose qname matches no node, mixed models, wrong dims) hold for any writer'; §3 ruling 3 (contract and validator first). At HEAD: code-domain/src/external_inputs.rs VectorRow {qname, kind?, hint?, model?, dims?, b64} with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]; check_vector checks only size vs dims; orphaned qnames are already a gaps row (engine/src/gaps.rs cell_rows, ORPHANED_CELL) and `glia cell ls --check` binds every vector row (cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs check_rows). Missing: mixed models, rows without model, dims disagreeing across rows, duplicate keys (the store keys vectors by qname alone, store/src/cells.rs Sidecar::upsert `rows.retain(|r| r.qname != w.qname)`, so a CLASS and its same-qname SERVICE collide), non-finite values, and the per-row text hash the freshness check and the embed cache need (FB.4, FB.5a). Engram's answer (engram-ask-0.5.4.md §5): `model` + `dims` required, naming the exact artifact; readers skip rows of another model.
entry_points: code-domain/src/external_inputs.rs - VectorRow gains `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub text_hash: Option<String>`; module doc ROWS paragraph rewritten as the contract

code-domain/src/external_inputs.rs - new `pub fn audit_vectors(rows: &[(u32, VectorRow)]) -> VectorAudit`, `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct VectorAudit { pub models: BTreeMap<String, usize>, pub issues: Vec<VectorIssue> }`, `pub struct VectorIssue { pub line: u32, pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub detail: String }`, `pub const VECTOR_ISSUES: [&str; 6]`, `pub fn vector_key(r: &VectorRow) -> (String, String)`

cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs - `ls --check` runs audit_vectors and lists issues
packets.implementation:
1. Contract (module doc + code): a vector row is `{"qname","kind"?,"hint"?,"model","dims","text_hash"?,"b64"}`; b64 = standard padded base64 of dims little-endian f32, unit-norm; one model per file; key (qname, kind). `text_hash` is `<recipe>:<16 lowercase hex>` (FB.4 defines recipes t1 / t2); a row without it is valid (another writer) and is never treated as fresh by glia's embed cache. Validation stays lenient on READ for old rows (model / dims stay Option in the struct so a 0.5.2 file loads); the audit reports them.
2. `vector_key(r) = (r.qname.clone(), r.kind.clone().unwrap_or_default())`. audit_vectors over (line, row) in file order: `no_model` (model None), `no_dims` (dims None), `mixed_model` (every row whose model is not the file's majority model; tie -> the lexicographically smallest model is the majority, so the verdict is deterministic), `dims_disagree` (a row whose dims differ from the first row of its model), `duplicate_key` (second and later rows of one vector_key), `bad_payload` (b64 undecodable, non-finite value, or |L2 norm - 1| > 1e-3; decode with a local f32 LE reader, no dependency on glia-embed). Issues sorted by (line, kind). VECTOR_ISSUES = [no_model, no_dims, mixed_model, dims_disagree, duplicate_key, bad_payload]. Also `pub fn text_hash_ok(s: &str) -> bool` (`t<digit>:<16 hex>`), used by bad_payload when text_hash is present but malformed.
3. store/src/cells.rs: Sidecar::upsert retains `vector_key(r) != key(w)`, take matches `(r.qname, kind)` (a CellRemoval's kind, "" when None: removing a kind-less row keeps rows that carry a kind), save sorts by vector_key. CellWrite::vector keeps its signature; a VECTOR upsert writes text_hash None (the cell API carries no text hash; FB.5a's bulk writer does).
4. cli `cell ls --check`: after check_rows, read the vector rows with their line numbers (`numbered` helper: the same `read_rows` order) and run audit_vectors; print one `issue <kind> .glia/vectors.jsonl:<line> qname=<q> <detail>` line per issue (in --json: top-level `vector_audit: {models, issues}`); exit 1 when any issue (as for a row that does not apply). Marker extended: `[cells] ls rows=.. ` line gains ` vector_issues=<n> models=<m>` (m = distinct models).
5. Tests (engine/tests/cell_write_api.rs): a CLASS and SERVICE sharing a qname each keep their own VECTOR row through two writes (failed at HEAD: the second write replaced the first); audit unit tests in external_inputs.rs mod tests: each of the six issue kinds from a hand-built file, majority tie-break, a clean 3-row file -> no issue. cli/tests/cell_cli.rs: `glia cell ls --check` on a sidecar with a mixed-model row exits 1 and prints `issue mixed_model`.
6. docs/overlay.md (the sidecar section that documents vectors.jsonl): the contract table and the six issue kinds.
7. Committed fixture (§3 ruling 3, a writer-agnostic sidecar): cli/tests/data/vectors/foreign_writer.jsonl, three rows as another writer would write them (model Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5, dims 4 so the file stays small, no text_hash, one row with `kind`, one with `hint`), unit-norm payloads; cell_cli.rs copies it into a scratch repo and `ls --check` reports zero vector issues; a second fixture line appended in the test with another model gives `issue mixed_model`.
packets.acceptance: `cargo test -p glia-code-domain --lib external_inputs`, `cargo test -p glia-store`, `cargo test -p glia-engine --test cell_write_api --test external_cells`, `cargo test -p glia-cli --test cell_cli` and cli_surface green (regenerate cli/surface/cell.txt only if help text moved); clippy -D warnings clean. packets.title: Vectors are query-time, not a build input: the build stops applying `.glia/vectors.jsonl` as VECTOR cells, the layout fingerprint and watch's durability skip it, and a VECTOR write through the cell API writes the sidecar only (`write_through=sidecar_only`)
packets.area: FB embeddings: the sidecar leaves the build
packets.rationale: At HEAD `.glia/vectors.jsonl` is a build input three ways: engine/src/external/cells.rs apply_sidecar applies every row as a VECTOR cell, store/src/layout.rs external_inputs_fingerprint hashes it (so writing it makes the next load_or_rebuild rebuild the whole graph), and engine/src/watch.rs durability() calls it High(glia_inputs) (a re-plan). With `glia embed` writing it (FB.5a) and `glia watch --embed` writing it after each update (FB.10), that is a rebuild per embed and a watch that re-plans on its own write (the repo-graph watcher-loop class of bug). It also carries 384 x 4 = 1,536 bytes per node into every layout and every held PyGraph (about 47 MB for glia's 31k nodes) although no answer reads VECTOR cells at HEAD (grep: only external/cells.rs, gaps.rs, the cell CLI / py writers and store tests touch cell_type::VECTOR). The semantic tier reads the sidecar itself (FB.4), with the model and text hash the cell drops (graph/src/cells.rs stores CellPayload::Bytes only). Snapshot steps never run inside a build (binding rule); a sidecar a build ignores is the same rule's read side.
entry_points: engine/src/external/cells.rs - apply_sidecar reads CELLS_FILE only; the vector loop and VECTORS_FILE import go
store/src/layout.rs - external_inputs_fingerprint skips `.glia/vectors.jsonl` (new `fn is_query_time_input(rel: &str) -> bool`, also used for FB.13a's vocab dir)

1. code-domain stays as is (VECTORS_FILE keeps its path). engine/src/external/cells.rs apply_sidecar: read and apply CELLS_FILE rows only; the `[cells] sidecar` marker's per-type counts keep `VECTOR=0` (WRITABLE unchanged) and gain nothing; module doc: vectors are query-time (FB.4).

6. Tests: engine/tests/external_cells.rs - a repo with vectors.jsonl builds with no VECTOR cell and `[cells] sidecar ... VECTOR=0`; the layout stays fresh (`persist::load_or_rebuild` does not rebuild) after rewriting vectors.jsonl, and goes stale after rewriting cells.jsonl (control). engine/tests/cell_write_api.rs: VECTOR write -> sidecar row, outcome write_through sidecar_only, layout bytes unchanged. watch: a mod test applying `.glia/vectors.jsonl` is a noop (no re-plan, `[watch] noop`).

packets.area: FB embeddings: what is embedded and how it is read
packets.rationale: §B: embed 'name, qname, leading_doc and code ... Engram measured full text beating name + qname 78 vs 54 of 100'; Engram's text is name, qname, leading doc (500-char cap) and up to 10 imports not already in name + qname, never a code body, and 'Code bodies were never measured: the spec run A/Bs them' with 'code goes LAST' (fastembed truncates at 512 tokens, fastembed-4.9.1 DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH 512). So two recipes, t1 (Engram's) and t2 (t1 + code), both shipped and measured by FB.6, which picks the default. The leading doc is the DOC cell (code-domain cell_type::DOC, read by projection-text ladder `first_text(n, DOC)`), the imports the IMPORTS cell (cell 16: 'External library names imported in a node's source file', the field engram-export fills Content::Symbol.imports from), the code the CODE cell. A reader 'skips rows whose model differs from its query model' (§B). The index is what the semantic tier (FB.7a, FB.8, FB.9), the embed run's cache (FB.5a) and the gate harness (FB.6) share, so the measured text is the shipped text.

1. code-domain/src/profile.rs: `pub const EMBED_KINDS: &[NodeKindId]` = MODULE, CLASS, FUNCTION, METHOD, ROUTE, INTERFACE, STRUCT, ENDPOINT, ENUM, GRPC_SERVICE, QUEUE_CONSUMER, QUEUE_PRODUCER, GRAPHQL_RESOLVER, GRAPHQL_OPERATION, WS_HANDLER, EVENT_HANDLER, CLI_COMMAND, COMPONENT, HOOK, SERVICE, DIRECTIVE, PIPE, GUARD, COMPOSABLE, DATA_ENTITY, CRON_JOB, STATE_VAR, DOC_SECTION, MESSAGE_TYPE, RPC_PROCEDURE (declarations, channel ends a person names, docs); doc comment: a new embeddable kind is one row here (CLAUDE.md: tables, never a list in a consumer).
2. text.rs: node data read from the first graph holding the id (find's rule): name and qname from nav, kind from nav.kind_by_id (None or not in EMBED_KINDS -> embed_text None). doc = first DOC cell text, whitespace-collapsed, cut at 500 chars on a char boundary. imports = the IMPORTS cell's JSON array, in its stored order, keeping names not contained (ASCII-case-insensitive) in name or qname, first 10, joined by ' '. code = first CODE cell text (a CodeSpan reads back as text through the store; a span that did not resolve - `{"code_span":..}` JSON - counts as no code), cut at 4000 chars. t1 = lines [name, qname, doc?, imports?] joined by '\n', empty parts omitted; t2 = t1 + '\n' + code when code is present (code LAST). text_hash = format!("{}:{}", r.as_str(), first 16 hex of blake3(text)) (blake3 is already an engine dependency, CE.2a). RECIPES = [T1, T2]. `pub const DEFAULT_RECIPE: EmbedRecipe` = T1 until FB.6's report picks (FB.6 edits this const if t2 wins).
3. index.rs: VectorIndex::load: for each (repo, root) in key order, read `root/.glia/vectors.jsonl` with read_rows::<VectorRow>, keep rows whose model == `model` (count the others as `other_model`), decode with glia_embed::codec::from_le_bytes (row dims or the first kept row's dims; a row of other dims or bad payload -> `bad`), bind through glia_graph::cells::QnameIndex::build(merged, Some(RepoId(repo))).resolve(qname, kind, hint) (Bound / Rekeyed bind; Ambiguous / Orphaned -> `unbound`). For every bound row compare row.text_hash with text_hash(recipe, embed_text(id)): equal -> fresh (kept), different or absent -> `stale` (not kept: it embeds other text). Then every node of EMBED_KINDS in that repo with no fresh vector is `missing` (`missing_ids()` returns them sorted by (qname, NodeId), the embed run's and the inline embedder's work list). Vectors kept in a dense Vec<f32> (n x dims) with a parallel Vec<NodeId>, sorted by (qname, NodeId) so iteration order is fixed. search: cosine = dot (rows and query are unit; renormalise the query), skip `exclude`, keep the top_k by (similarity desc, qname asc, NodeId asc) with a bounded sorted Vec; SemanticHit { id, similarity: f64 (rounded to 4 decimals for output only, compared unrounded) }. IndexStats { model, recipe, dims, rows, fresh, stale, missing, other_model, unbound, bad }. Marker per load: `[semantic] index repos=<r> model=<m> recipe=<t> dims=<d> rows=<n> fresh=<f> stale=<s> missing=<x> other_model=<o> unbound=<u> bad=<b> ms=<t>`. A repo with no sidecar contributes missing only. No HashMap iteration reaches any output.
4. Tests (engine/tests/semantic_index.rs, a tmp repo built with generate_one; vectors written with glia_embed::HashEmbedder over embed_text): t1 / t2 texts for a documented Python function (doc capped, imports filtered, code last in t2 only); a row with another model -> other_model; a row whose text_hash is stale after editing the function's docstring -> stale and listed in missing_ids; search ranks the function whose text shares the query's words first; ties (two identical texts) ordered by qname; two loads give identical stats and order; a node kind outside EMBED_KINDS (PROJECT) never counted.

Each vector is cached by a hash of its text, so a re-run embeds only changed nodes; rows carry `model` and `dims`'; Engram's gotchas (never embed concurrently with a build's rayon pool; cache dir never a repo dir). 1. EmbedOptions (#[non_exhaustive], Default): recipe (DEFAULT_RECIPE), replace: bool (false), limit: Option<usize> (embed at most n missing nodes; None all), check_only: bool (count, write nothing). EmbedReport { model, recipe, dims, nodes (EMBED_KINDS nodes of the repo), cached (fresh rows kept), reused (missing nodes whose text hash matched a vector already in the file under another key: a moved / renamed node), embedded, stale_dropped (rows bound to no node any more or superseded), foreign_kept (rows of this model glia did not write: no text_hash, kept untouched), rows_written, ms }.
2. embed_repo(root: &Path, merged: &MergedGraph, repo: RepoId, embedder: &dyn Embedder, opts) -> Result<EmbedReport, String>: (a) read existing rows; if any row's model != embedder.model() and !replace -> Err("<file> holds vectors of model <m>; pass --replace to rewrite it with <model>") (one model per file, FB.2). (b) VectorIndex::load for this repo (model, recipe) -> fresh rows + missing_ids. (c) cache: text_hash -> bytes from every existing row of this model that has a text_hash. (d) for each missing id in missing_ids order: text = embed_text; h = text_hash; cache hit -> reused, else queue (text, id). Apply limit to the queue. (e) embed the queue in chunks of glia_embed::CHUNK sequentially (one call per chunk; never inside a rayon scope: embed_repo asserts `rayon::current_thread_index().is_none()` and returns Err otherwise, documenting Engram's thrash finding), progress marker every chunk `[embed] chunk <i>/<n> texts=<k> ms=<t>`. (f) rows = fresh rows (unchanged bytes) + new rows {qname, kind: NodeKind NAME, hint: graph::identity hint of the node (the v1 form the cell store uses; None when the node has none), model, dims, text_hash, b64} + foreign_kept; drop rows of this model whose node is gone or whose text changed (stale_dropped). (g) unless check_only, write_vector_rows(root, rows, mode). Determinism: rows sorted by vector_key; the same tree, model and cache give byte-identical files (no timestamps in rows).
3. store write_vector_rows: take CellsLock, re-read the file (a row another writer added since step (a) and of another model is an Err under MergeSameModel), write sorted rows with write_rows (tmp + rename), return the count. `.glia/.gitignore` already lists vectors.jsonl (snapshots/src/lib.rs GLIA_GITIGNORE); create `.glia/` if absent but never the gitignore here (history sync owns it).
4. Marker at the end: `[embed] repo=<label> model=<m> recipe=<t> nodes=<n> cached=<c> reused=<r> embedded=<e> stale_dropped=<s> foreign_kept=<f> rows=<w> ms=<t>`.

The semantic tier reaches find / flow search / pack's fallback only if it beats BM25 alone on the gate; otherwise glia embed ships as a sidecar with no answer reading it, and the report says so.' The gate's repos are 0.5.3 EG.3's pinned public snapshots (bench/rank-gate/snapshots.json: glia v0.5.2, pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples); the find shape and BM25-alone (T1s, past commit messages -> files) are rank_eval's R3_SHAPES `find` bank (engine/examples/rank_eval.rs r3_transfer, ans_keys_find), the statistics EG.2's `paired` commit-cluster bootstrap. packets.implementation:
1. Node vectors: for each recipe in semantic::RECIPES, the texts of every EMBED_KINDS node of ctx.merged (`semantic::embed_text`), keyed by text_hash; a cache file `<sem_cache>/<label>-<model-slug>.jsonl` (`{"h":<text_hash>,"b64":..}` rows) so a re-run embeds only new texts; embed misses with glia_embed::named(sem_model) sequentially (bge-small needs the build's `--features sem-eval`; without it named() errs and rank_eval exits 2 naming the feature; test-hash always works) (rank_eval's own pools are idle at this point: build it before any rayon work of the query loop, or embed in the main thread before r3_transfer). Rand control: per node a unit vector from the harness's `Rng` seeded with h64(qname) (dims = model dims), identical across runs.
2. Query vectors: the test commit's subject (the find shape's query, as ans_keys_find uses), embedded raw (SEM:*) and with the BGE prefix `Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ` (SEMp:t1 only), cached by text in the same file.
3. Seed exclusion and candidate files exactly as the find bank's other rankers. Marker: `[sem-eval] label=<l> recipe=<r> nodes=<n> embedded=<e> cached=<c> queries=<q> ms=<t>`.

FUSE[T1s,SEM:r*] - T1s is reported beside it as information only (a fused find --files would need its own packet and James's ruling). PASS = R1 and R2. The report lists every row (repo, ranker pair, diff, CI), the verdict, r*, the query form, wall times (node embed, query embed) and the t2 index-load cost; aggregate numbers only (public repos).

packets.title: When embeds run: `glia watch --embed` embeds the changed / un-embedded nodes after each emitted update (same thread, after the build, debounced by the update), and `glia install-hooks --embed` adds `glia embed .` to the post-commit / post-merge hooks; the explicit `glia embed` and FB.7a's inline threshold are the other two triggers
packets.area: FB embeddings: embed triggers
packets.rationale: §B 'When embeds run (James: we could have a way to determine when to run the embeds) ... Candidates for the spec run: glia watch embeds changed nodes in the background after an apply, debounced; install-hooks adds a post-commit / post-merge glia embed; a semantic query ... embeds them inline under a small threshold ... an explicit glia embed always works. A [embed] marker reports embedded / cached / stale counts.' Decision here: all four, each opt-in except the explicit command and the inline threshold (FB.7a, 64 nodes, writes nothing). Watch runs the embed on its own loop thread after the update is emitted, so it never overlaps a build's rayon pool (Engram's thrash finding); FB.3 makes the sidecar Low durability so the write does not re-plan the watch. The sidecar ships whatever FB.6 says (item 13: 'otherwise glia embed ships as a sidecar'), so this packet is not gated.

packets.title: Corrections reach answers: pack's ladder renders a node's DECISION / CONV entries (writer, id, text; HEURISTIC for api-sourced rows) at Outline and above, the pack manifest counts them, and `glia cell ls --rekey` leaves rows in another writer's id namespace (`<writer>:` ids such as `engram:`) unless `--writer <ns>` names it
packets.area: FB Engram data: corrections as cells
packets.rationale: §B 'Corrections as cells: IN 0.5.4 ... judged on glia's side by whether the cells improve answers ... glia's side already exists: the LF.1 sidecar and the orphaned_cell gaps row. Agreed lifetime rule for any writer: the writer owns its rows, glia never deletes another source's rows, an orphan is kept, reported and attached to nothing, and the writer re-anchors or deletes it on its next write'; engram-ask-0.5.4.md §2 item 1 'glia shows them as HEURISTIC'. Checked at HEAD: the write surfaces, hint, lock, ids and orphan reporting exist (see the dropped list); but NO answer reads DECISION / CONV cells (grep cell_type::DECISION / CONV in engine/src finds only adr.rs, profile.rs and external/declared.rs, which write them; projection-text/src/ladder.rs renders only DOC and CODE text), so a correction cannot improve any answer today. pack is the answer that hands context to agents (CC.4b). And `glia cell ls --rekey` (cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs rekey_rows) rewrites ANY rekeyed row, Engram's included, which the lifetime rule reserves to the writer (engram-ask §5: Engram re-anchors its own rows at each consolidate).
entry_points: projection-text/src/ladder.rs - render_node: a `notes` block for Outline / Preview / Full (new `fn notes_of(n: &Node) -> Vec<Note>` over DECISION and CONV cells)
engine/src/pack.rs - PackedNode gains `notes: usize` (skipped when 0); the [pack] marker gains ` notes=<n>`
cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs - rekey_rows skips namespaced ids not named by `--writer`
packets.implementation:
1. ladder.rs: notes_of(n) = every entry of the node's DECISION cells then CONV cells (each cell is a JSON array of entries, external_inputs module doc PAYLOADS), skipping CONV entries whose `kind` is `convention` (FB.12b renders those) and DECISION entries the overlay's `[[decision]]` scope stanzas anchored on a PROJECT (they are scope records, kept out of per-node text); sorted by (source, id). Render at Outline+ after the doc line: one line per note, at most 3 then `(+k more notes)`: `note[<source>/<id>, <tier>]: <title or text, whitespace-collapsed, cut at 200 chars>` where tier is `heuristic` for source api (a writer's statement: Engram's corrections), `declared` for overlay / adr. Qname rung: none. Full and Preview of a node with no CODE (rendered_as) keep the notes (they render as Outline). Token cost follows from render_node (pack's climb already measures it).
2. pack.rs: PackedNode.notes = notes_of count for packed nodes rendered at Outline+ (0 otherwise); marker ` notes=<sum>`. py/api_surface/pack.txt regenerated only if the PackedNode dict keys are pinned there.
3. cell.rs --rekey: a row whose entry id contains ':' before any other char class (regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:`) has writer namespace = that prefix; rekey rewrites it only when `--writer <ns>` equals it; other namespaced rekeyed rows are listed with status `rekeyed` and `[cells] rekey skipped foreign=<n> (writer owns its rows; --writer <ns> to rewrite)`. Rows with un-namespaced ids (glia's own CLI / py writes, `000001`, overlay / adr ids) rekey as before. Module doc: the lifetime rule. Regenerate cli/surface/cell.txt.
4. Tests: engine/tests/pack_notes.rs - a cells.jsonl DECISION `{"source":"api","id":"engram:3f2a","text":"keep charge_card idempotent"}` on a function: `glia pack <fn>` text shows `note[api/engram:3f2a, heuristic]: keep charge_card idempotent`, PackedNode.notes 1; four notes -> 3 lines + `(+1 more notes)`; a node without notes renders byte-identically to HEAD (ladder unit test). cli/tests/cell_cli.rs - a moved node with an `engram:` row and a `000001` row: `ls --rekey` rewrites only the second and prints `rekey skipped foreign=1`; `--writer engram` rewrites both.

packets.title: Scope-level conventions: overlay `[[convention]]` (`scope` = path / project label, or `component` = a reflexion-model component; `text`; `by`), legal in overlay versions 1 and 2, stored as a CONV entry `{"kind":"convention","scope","scope_raw","component"?}` on the constraint anchor rule (DT.7a), and accepted from the cell API so Engram can write one
packets.area: FB Engram data: scope-level conventions
packets.rationale: §B 'Spec item: scope-level conventions. In glia, CONV is a free-text note on ONE node (overlay [[note]]) ... A convention that covers a scope (modals are centred, never bottom-anchored: every modal component) has no home ... The spec run decides whether a convention attaches to a module / component / project scope (the reflexion model's components are a candidate anchor) and which answers show it.' Decision: a convention names a scope by path or project label (the [[constraint]] scope grammar, resolved once to a repo-relative path, `scope` / `scope_raw` as constraint entries store them) or by a reflexion-model component (its declared paths); it is stored where a scoped [[constraint]] anchors (engine/src/external/declared.rs Anchors::rule_anchor: the PROJECT at the path, else the enclosing PROJECT, else the smallest-id MODULE under it), and every node whose located file is under the scope is governed by it (FB.12b shows it). CONV keeps the cell type (no registry id needed: an entry `kind` field distinguishes it, as CONSTRAINT entries carry `kind`). The overlay schema change follows 0.5.3 EB.4's precedent for `[ids]` (legal in versions 1 and 2).
entry_points: code-domain/src/glia_config.rs - `pub struct ConventionDecl { id: Option<String>, scope: Option<String>, component: Option<String>, text: String, by: Option<String> }` (deny_unknown_fields; exactly one of scope / component), GliaConfig gains `convention: Vec<Spanned<ConventionDecl>>`, SECTIONS gains "convention"
engine/src/external/declared.rs - stanzas(): a `convention` section -> CONV entry; anchored by rule_anchor (scope) or the component's anchor; orphaned / rejected through the existing Unbound reasons
code-domain/src/external_inputs.rs - validate_entry accepts a CONV entry with `kind: "convention"` only with a non-empty `scope` string (and optional `component`)
docs/overlay.md - the [[convention]] section
packets.implementation:
1. glia_config.rs: ConventionDecl; loader check: exactly one of scope / component (`[[convention]] needs exactly one of scope or component`), text non-empty and <= MAX_NOTE_CHARS, id (default `convention#<n>`, 1-based) <= MAX_ID_CHARS. Legal in versions 1 and 2 (no version gate). SECTIONS length +1 ("convention" last, after EB.4's "ids"); section_counts counts it; `[overlay] config` marker prints `convention=<n>`.
2. declared.rs stanzas(): for each convention, entry = object([source overlay, id, kind "convention", scope (resolved path via Anchors::path_of; for a component, its first resolved path), scope_raw (as written), component (name, when given), paths (a component's every resolved path, else [scope]), text (redacted like notes), by, decl]); target = Target::Scope for a scope (bound with rule_anchor's Via, counted in anchor_enclosing etc. like a scoped constraint) and the component's anchor for a component (component_anchor; an unknown component -> rejected `no [[component]] named <c>`). Tally gains `convention`; the `[declared] repo=..` line gains ` convention=<n>` after note=. A convention is a record, not a rule: declared_misses does not list it (as decisions / notes).
3. external_inputs.rs validate_entry for CONV: if entry.kind == "convention", require `scope` (non-empty string) and allow `paths` (array of strings), `component`, `scope_raw`; a CONV entry with another `kind` is rejected (`CONV kind must be absent or "convention"`). Engram writes `{"source":"api","id":"engram:<hash>","kind":"convention","scope":"frontend/src/app/modals","text":".."}` on the scope's anchor qname through `glia cell set` (documented in docs/overlay.md and the module doc).
4. Tests (engine/tests/declared_cells.rs): `[[convention]] scope = "web"` (a project label) anchors on the web PROJECT with scope `apps/web`; scope = a sub-directory of a project anchors on the enclosing PROJECT (anchor_enclosing); component = "ui" anchors on the component's anchor with paths = the component's paths; both scope and component -> rejected with the message; a version-1 file with [[convention]] loads; a cell-API CONV with kind convention and no scope -> rejected.
packets.acceptance: `cargo test -p glia-code-domain` and `cargo test -p glia-engine --test declared_cells --test check_declared --test user_config_walk` green; clippy clean; docs/overlay.md documents the section.
