packets.title: Conventions in answers: `engine::conventions_for` (pub(crate)) gives the conventions governing a file (longest scope first); pack renders a `## conventions` section for its packed nodes' files and review a `### Conventions` section (dict key `conventions`) for the changed files, each row with its scope, writer and decl
packets.area: FB Engram data: scope-level conventions in answers
packets.rationale: §B 'which answers show it' - decided: pack (the context an agent works from) and review (the PR report: a change inside a scope should be checked against its conventions, e.g. 'modals are centred' for a change under the modal components). find / blast-radius rows stay node answers (no free-text attachments). The conventions are stored by FB.12a as CONV entries on anchors; a reader collects them once per answer and matches a file by repo-relative path prefix against `paths` (the A8.3 `/`-boundary rule, answers::in_scope).
entry_points: engine/src/external/declared.rs - `pub(crate) struct Convention { repo: u64, id, source, text, scope, component: Option<String>, paths: Vec<String>, by: Option<String>, decl: Option<String> }`, `pub(crate) fn conventions(merged: &MergedGraph) -> Vec<Convention>`, `pub(crate) fn conventions_for<'a>(all: &'a [Convention], repo: u64, file: &str) -> Vec<&'a Convention>`
engine/src/pack.rs - Pack gains `conventions: Vec<PackConvention>` (skipped when empty); render appends `## conventions`
engine/src/review.rs - Review gains `conventions: Vec<ReviewConvention>`; render_markdown `### Conventions`
packets.implementation:
1. conventions(merged): scan every node's CONV cells for entries with kind "convention" (any source), dedupe by (repo, source, id), sort by (repo, scope, source, id). conventions_for: those of the file's repo whose any `paths` entry is a `/`-boundary prefix of the file ("." covers all), sorted by longest matching path desc then (source, id).
2. pack: after the picks are final, the distinct files of packed nodes -> the union of their conventions (sorted as above, deduped), as `PackConvention { id, source, tier ("declared" overlay / "heuristic" api), scope, text, decl, files: usize }` (files = how many packed files it governs); rendered after the node sections as `## conventions` then `- <text> (scope <scope>, <source>/<id>)`; the section's bytes count toward the budget like the links section (re-render loop unchanged: the section is fixed text measured in the total). Marker ` conventions=<n>` on the [pack] line.
3. review: the changed files (Review's changed rows' files) -> conventions with the changed files each governs; `Review.conventions` (serialised, skipped when empty), markdown `### Conventions` table `| convention | scope | files changed | source |` after the impact section; never blocking (a convention is not a rule). Marker `[review] conventions=<n>`.
4. py: PyGraph.pack dicts and review_vs_rev dicts gain the keys when non-empty (convert.rs handles the serialisable structs); regenerate py/api_surface pack / review only if keys are pinned; test_review.py pins `conventions` presence for a fixture.
5. Tests (engine/tests/conventions_answers.rs): overlay `[[convention]] scope = "src/modals" text = "modals are centred"`; pack of a node in src/modals/confirm.ts shows the section, of a node elsewhere does not; a nested convention (src/modals/legacy) sorts first for a file under it; review of a change touching src/modals/confirm.ts lists it with files changed 1 and exit code unchanged (0); an api-sourced convention renders tier heuristic.

packets.title: The identifier vocabulary snapshot: `glia_snapshots::vocab_sync(root, rev)` reads every tracked text file at the git index of a commit (everything the build filters included), tokenises `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` of 3+ chars, and writes `.glia/vocab-snapshot/{files.jsonl, vocab.jsonl, meta.json}` with Engram's row shapes; `code_domain::snapshots::read_vocab` reads it
packets.area: FB Engram data: the vocabulary index
packets.rationale: §B 'Engram ask: the repo's identifier vocabulary ... Endorsed 2026-10-16 (James: sick good gaps coverage and enhancements for glia): the vocabulary index is a glia substrate feature first, with Engram's --vocab export as one reader of it.' Settled with Engram: tracked = the git index at the commit (like-for-like with its git grep; untracked files would break cross-clone identity); every identifier-like token, 3+ chars, including everything the export filters; rows `{"t","files":[ids],"n"}` with files capped at 16 (`"common": true` past it), path rows `{"f","path"}`, sorted by token. Measured on glia: 3,640 text files, 52,764 tokens, 2.7 MB JSONL. Snapshot steps never run inside a build and the snapshots crate is 'the only crate that spawns a process' (Cargo.toml workspace comment).
entry_points: snapshots/src/vocab.rs (new) - `pub fn capture_vocab(repo_root: &Path, rev: &str) -> Result<Vocab, String>`, `pub use glia_code_domain::snapshots::vocab_tokens as tokens_of` (the pure tokeniser lives in code-domain so the engine can call it without the process-spawning crate)

snapshots/src/lib.rs - `mod vocab; pub use vocab::{capture_vocab, tokens_of};` and `pub fn vocab_sync(repo_root: &Path, opts: &VocabOptions) -> Result<VocabSummary, String>`; GLIA_GITIGNORE gains `vocab-snapshot/`

code-domain/src/snapshots.rs - VOCAB_DIR, VocabMeta, VocabFile, VocabToken, `vocab_tokens`, `write_vocab`, `read_vocab(root) -> Option<VocabSnapshot>`, `VocabSnapshot::files_of(token) -> Option<VocabHit>`
packets.implementation:
1. capture_vocab: `git -C root ls-tree -r -z --name-only <rev>` (the commit's tree = the index at that commit; `rev` default HEAD), then one `git cat-file --batch` process fed `<rev>:<path>` lines (spawned like git_history.rs's Command use). Text files only: skip a blob containing a NUL byte in its first 8000 bytes (git's own binary heuristic) or larger than 4 MiB (counted `skipped_large`). code-domain `vocab_tokens(text: &[u8]) -> BTreeMap<String, u32>`: a byte scanner (ASCII; a non-ASCII byte ends a token) for `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, keep len >= 3, count occurrences. Files sorted by path, ids 0.. in that order. Per token: n = total occurrences, files = sorted file ids; if more than 16 files -> common = true and no list.
2. code-domain/src/snapshots.rs: VOCAB_DIR = "vocab-snapshot", VOCAB_VERSION = 1, files.jsonl rows `{"f":<id>,"path":"<repo-relative>"}`, vocab.jsonl rows `{"files":[..],"n":<n>,"t":"<tok>"}` / `{"common":true,"n":<n>,"t":"<tok>"}` (sorted keys, compact, sorted by token in byte order), meta.json `{version, rev (40 hex), files, tokens, common, skipped_binary, skipped_large, generator: "glia vocab sync", data_hash}` written LAST (the history snapshot's rule: a dir without meta is incomplete). write_vocab writes to a tmp dir and renames. read_vocab: None when meta is absent, version unknown or data_hash mismatches; VocabSnapshot holds tokens in a sorted Vec for binary search (no HashMap). files_of(t) -> VocabHit { n, files: Vec<String> (paths), common: bool }.
3. snapshots/src/lib.rs: VocabOptions { rev: Option<String> }, VocabSummary { rev, files, tokens, common, ms }; vocab_sync = capture + write_vocab + `.glia/.gitignore` creation as history_sync does (the const gains `vocab-snapshot/`; an existing .gitignore is never overwritten, so document that older repos should add the line). Marker `[vocab] sync rev=<12> files=<f> tokens=<t> common=<c> skipped_binary=<b> skipped_large=<l> ms=<ms>`.
4. The vocab dir is already a query-time input (FB.3's is_query_time_input / watch Low).
5. Tests (snapshots/tests/vocab.rs, a scratch git repo): tokens_of(b"fooBar x_y abc 9ab") = {abc:1, fooBar:1, x_y:1}... (x_y has 3 chars: kept); an untracked file is absent; a staged-but-uncommitted file is absent at rev HEAD; a binary file skipped; a token in 17 files is common with no list; two syncs of one commit from two clones at different paths are byte-identical; read_vocab round-trips; a truncated vocab.jsonl fails data_hash -> None.
packets.acceptance: `cargo test -p glia-snapshots --test vocab` and `cargo test -p glia-code-domain` green; clippy clean. packets.title: Named but not modelled: find's no_match absence names where an identifier of the query occurs (`named_in`: FACT, from the vocabulary snapshot) and gaps gains `named_not_modelled` rows for identifiers a markdown doc cites in code spans, that occur in tracked code files, but that no node names
packets.area: FB Engram data: vocabulary readers in glia
packets.rationale: §B: 'Substrate value beyond Engram: find's absence says no node named X, but X occurs in <files> (a FACT-tier named but not modelled signal), and gaps gains a named-but-not-modelled category over the same index.' A raw 'every token no node names' list would be dominated by locals, fields and keys (Engram: only 0.74 / 0.61 of what it flagged absent was truly absent because of exactly those names), so the gaps category is scoped to identifiers a repo's own docs cite in inline code (a doc that talks about `X`, X in code, no node X: a blind spot in the model the docs promise). Docs are DOC_SECTION nodes with their full text (CJ: full doc CODE text). The absence keeps find's FACT tier: 'X occurs in these tracked files' is read off the index.
entry_points: engine/src/absence.rs - Absence gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub named_in: Vec<NamedIn>` (`NamedIn { token, occurrences, files: Vec<String> /* <= 5 shown */, file_count, common }`)
engine/src/find.rs - find_nodes_with_live's absence closure fills named_in when the repo roots' vocab snapshots are given (`FindOptions.vocab_roots: Option<BTreeMap<u64, PathBuf>>`, default None)
engine/src/gaps.rs - `pub const NAMED_NOT_MODELLED: &str = "named_not_modelled";` CATEGORIES +1 (root category: needs the repo root)
packets.implementation:
1. Query tokens: the query's `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` tokens of 3+ chars (code-domain/src/snapshots.rs `vocab_tokens`, the pure tokeniser FB.13a defines there and snapshots' tokens_of re-exports: the engine never depends on the process-spawning snapshots crate). For a no_match absence with vocab_roots set: for each query token (in query order, deduped) that the vocab of any root holds -> NamedIn (files: the first 5 paths in path order, file_count, common); the absence note gains `; `X` occurs in <k> tracked file(s) (a.ts, b.ts, +n) but no node is named X`. No snapshot -> named_in empty and the note unchanged (HEAD bytes). Absence tier stays FACT.
2. gaps named_not_modelled (a ROOT category, it needs each repo's root): for each DOC_SECTION node (markdown) of the repo, its text's inline code spans (backtick pairs on one line, content an identifier or `Ident()` / `a.b` dotted - take the last segment), identifier-shaped (has an underscore or a lower->Upper step, or is PascalCase with 2+ humps; plain lowercase words are skipped as prose), not equal to any node's name in the repo (nav name_by_id set, built once), present in the vocab with >= 1 file whose extension is a code extension (code-domain's detect-language extension list; reuse `node_ext`'s reader on paths) -> one row per (repo, token): qname = token, kind = "identifier", file/line = the first doc citing it (path order, then line), detail = `repo=<l> cited by <d> doc section(s); occurs in <k> code file(s) (<first 3>); no node named <token>`, suggest = `check the parser for <ext> covers this declaration, or [[edge]] / [[note]] it in the overlay`, tier FACT. No vocab snapshot -> no rows, and gaps' summary prints `[gaps] named_not_modelled skipped: no vocab snapshot (run glia vocab sync) repo=<l>`. Marker `[gaps] named_not_modelled repo=<l> cited=<c> rows=<r>`.
3. Surfaces: CLI find / py find pass vocab_roots from their repo roots (always: the absence change is FACT and only appears with a snapshot); CLI gaps lists the category (regenerate cli/surface/gaps.txt if its help enumerates categories; `--category` accepts it). py api_surface find unchanged unless the Absence dict keys are pinned.
4. Tests (engine/tests/named_not_modelled.rs, scratch git repo + vocab_sync): README.md cites `retryBudget` and `parseTimeout`; `retryBudget` is a field inside a TS object literal (no node), `parseTimeout` a function (a node) -> one row for retryBudget, none for parseTimeout; a cited `the` word skipped; find('retryBudget') absence has named_in with the .ts file; without a snapshot the find absence JSON is byte-identical to HEAD. Code extensions: the engine's detect_language table (engine/src/extract.rs) is the one list of code extensions; gaps calls it on the path (detect_language(path).is_some()), never a copied list.
packets.acceptance: `cargo test -p glia-engine --test named_not_modelled --test gaps_report --test absence --test find_ranked` green; cli gaps / find tests and cli_surface green; clippy clean. INTEGRATOR (gaps category counts are relative): FC.9 (+4), FC.11 (+1) and FB.13c (+1) each add gaps categories in any order; this packet's CATEGORIES / GRAPH_CATEGORIES pins are HEAD's count +1 at its base, never the literal numbers in the text.

packets.area: FC - goal layer (code-domain)
packets.rationale: §G: one generalized intermediate connector between goal-layer units (requirement, task, decision row, spec section, ruling, packet) and code, with tiered links and lineage reusing the 0.5.2 identity classes; §F item 8's remaining half makes task / intent / plan nodes first-class. Every later FC packet needs one shared vocabulary that the build, the store and the answers agree on: what a unit is, the role a mention plays (shape rule 2), the key types each resolver owns (shape rule 7 gates per key type) and a qname that is never a bare id (shape rule 1: reused bare D1-D12 across four series was the weakest route in dev-notes/keys-eval-glia-2026-10-18.md). The registry ids themselves are F0's (code-domain/src/lib.rs); this packet fills the code-domain `goal` slot and the profile / identity tables. Lineage = an identity class (§G 'lineage = identity classes'), so it is one more `same_as` rule, written by the goal join pass (FC.5b) the way DT.1h's models pass writes http_model.

packets.implementation:
Builds on F0's ids: node_kind::GOAL_UNIT (50), edge_category::TRACES (38), cell_type::UNIT (26) and the code-domain `pub mod goal;` slot. If F0 picked other numbers, use its names; never a raw id here.
1. code-domain/src/goal.rs: `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum UnitKind { Requirement, Task, Decision, Ruling, Spec, Packet, Instrument, Milestone, Pr, Issue, Item }` with `as_str` and `pub const UNIT_KINDS: [UnitKind; 11]` in that order (the marker order). `pub enum Role { Defines, Cites, NamesFile, Supersedes, Implements, Requires }` (same derives) with `pub fn rule(self, state: Option<&str>) -> String`: `names_file/pending`, `names_file/done`, `names_file` (no state) for NamesFile, the snake name otherwise; `pub fn parse_rule(rule: &str) -> Option<(Role, Option<&str>)>` (the inverse, a `/<route>` suffix on `cites` kept as the route). `pub enum KeyType { Path, ScopedId, Lineage, Citation, Url, Endpoint, Qname }` + `KEY_TYPES` (gate strata order). §G's 'table row' key is an id DEFINED by a table row (EB.5a's rule: first cell equals the id) and resolved by the scoped-id resolver, so it is a unit SOURCE, not a mention key: `pub enum RowSource { List, Table, Heading, Tracker, Adr, Instrument, Gh, History, Citation }` (same derives; `as_str`), carried on every unit so FC.6 gates table-defined units as their own stratum. `pub enum UnitState { Pending, Done, Open, Closed, Superseded }` serialised snake_case.
2. The UNIT cell payload, JSON, `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`: `pub struct UnitCell { pub unit: UnitKind, pub source: RowSource, pub id: String, pub ns: String, #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if=..)] pub state: Option<UnitState>, pub title: String /* <= 200 chars, cut at a char boundary */, pub page: String, pub line: u32 /* 1-based */, pub digest: String /* 16 hex, xxh64 of the row's head text: a reworded row is a changed unit for FC.8's --base mode */, #[serde(default, ..)] pub version: Option<String>, #[serde(default)] pub mentions: Vec<MentionCell> /* <= 256, sorted by (line, key, text) */, #[serde(default)] pub cited_by: Vec<CiteCell> /* <= 512, sorted by (file, line) */, #[serde(default, ..)] pub cited_total: Option<u32> /* set only when cited_by was capped */ }`; `pub struct MentionCell { pub key: KeyType, pub text: String, pub role: Role, pub line: u32, #[serde(default, ..)] pub state: Option<UnitState> }`; `pub struct CiteCell { pub file: String, pub line: u32, pub route: String, pub tier: String /* fact|derived|heuristic */ }`. `UnitCell::to_cell(&self) -> Cell` (CellPayload::Json, kind UNIT) and `pub fn parse_unit_cell(c: &Cell) -> Option<UnitCell>` (None for another kind or a payload that does not parse; never panics). Use the xxhash64 code-domain already links (`twox-hash`, the hash `snapshots::data_hash` and code_span.rs use: seed 0) for `digest`; no new crate.
3. `pub fn unit_qname(ns: &str, id: &str) -> Result<String, &'static str>` = `goal:<ns>#<id>`; Err(`bare id`) when ns is empty or equals id (shape rule 1: a unit never has a bare qname), Err(`bad id`) when id is empty, longer than 128 chars or holds `#` or a control char. `pub const EMITTER_UNITS: &str = "goal:units"` (the repo-stage unit graph, FC.4) and `pub const EMITTER_JOIN: &str = "goal:join"` (the Post pass, FC.5b): a new EVIDENCE emitter STAGE `goal`, read by FC.5b's why.rs row. `pub const GOAL_GRAPH_LABEL: &str = "goal"`. `pub fn is_goal_edge(c: EdgeCategoryId) -> bool` (TRACES) and `pub fn is_goal_kind(k: NodeKindId) -> bool` (GOAL_UNIT): the ONE helper pair every code-answer reader filters through (FC.5b), defined here so no later packet edits this file for it.
4. code-domain/src/same_as.rs: `pub const RULE_ID_LINEAGE: &str = "id_lineage";`, `pub const GOAL_RULES: [&str; 1] = [RULE_ID_LINEAGE];`, `ALL_RULES: [&str; 11]` = RULES then MODEL_RULES then GOAL_RULES (the existing doc comment extended), `IDENTITY_EMITTERS: [&str; 3]` gains `goal::EMITTER_JOIN`. Fix every fixed-size use (`grep -rn ALL_RULES engine cli py`; `glia identity --rule` and `by_rule` read the array, so they list id_lineage last with no other edit).
5. code-domain/src/profile.rs CODE_TABLES: `(ec::TRACES, 0.0)` beside `(ec::SAME_AS, 0.0)` in activation_weights and in every preset's override list where SAME_AS has a row; TRACES gets community weight 0 exactly as SAME_AS: `community_weight` returns 0 for an unlisted category, so this is one `// TRACES out: ..` comment line beside the `// SAME_AS out` one, never a row; TRACES is in no carry_edges / effect_sinks list; GOAL_UNIT is in no entry kind list. identity_rules gains, after the two models rows: `IdentityRule { name: same_as::RULE_ID_LINEAGE, from: &[nk::GOAL_UNIT], to: &[nk::GOAL_UNIT], key: "one id renumbered / renamed / split one-to-one (a lineage phrase on its defining row)", tier: IdentityTier::Derived, walk: true }` with a comment that the goal join pass writes it (IdentityResolver reads `CODE_TABLES.identity_rule(<name>)` by name and never iterates the table (graph/src/resolvers/identity.rs, DD.3), so it needs no edit; a test asserts a build writes no `id_lineage` SAME_AS from `resolver:identity`).

Globs go through EB.4's `PathGlobs::new`. Legal in versions 1 and 2. `SECTIONS` is unchanged (they are inside `[ids]`).
2. code-domain/src/goal.rs: `pub const DEFAULT_KINDS: [(&str, UnitKind); 6] = [("T", Task), ("FR-", Requirement), ("NFR-", Requirement), ("SC-", Requirement), ("REQ-", Requirement), ("ADR-", Decision)]`; `pub fn kind_of(family: &str, page: &str, heading_words: &str, kinds: &[KindDecl]) -> UnitKind`: a declared family wins, then DEFAULT_KINDS, then the heading words (`decision` -> Decision, `ruling` -> Ruling, `requirement` -> Requirement, `task` -> Task), then a page under `specs/` or `features/` named `spec.md` -> Spec, else Item. Pure; the order is the doc's table.
3. The citation grammar: `pub const DEFAULT_SECTION_SHAPES: [&str; 7] = ["s {S}", "section {S}", "sections {S}", "§{S}", "art. {S}", "article {S}", "reg {S}"]` where `{S}` = digits, optional uppercase letters, then zero or more `(<digits><optional lowercase>)` / `(<lowercase roman>)` groups (`12`, `12A`, `12(3)(b)`); a shape matches case-insensitively at word boundaries; `sections 12-14` / `ss 12 and 13` yield each section. `pub struct Citation { pub instrument: Option<String>, pub version: Option<String>, pub section: String, pub start: usize, pub end: usize, pub how: &'static str /* alias_line | alias_near | page_default | none */ }` and `pub fn citations(line: &str, instruments: &[InstrumentDecl], page_default: Option<&str>) -> Vec<Citation>`: every section match; its instrument = the alias match on the same line nearest to it (`alias_line`, ties to the earlier alias), else `page_default` (`page_default`), else None (`none`); its version = a 4-digit year or a declared version string adjacent to that alias (within 12 bytes after it: `Example Act 2019`, `Example Regulations (v3)`) when it names a declared version, else None (the instrument's current version applies at resolution, FC.5a). No regex crate needed: a byte scanner like EB.4's IdPattern matcher. Sorted by start.

2. `GoalResolvers::new(merged: &MergedGraph, roots: &BTreeMap<u64, String>)` builds once: one EA.3 `rank::FileIndex` over the merged graph and per repo its EB.3 view `Candidates::of(&files, repo)` (the 0.5.3 integrator note: one candidate file space; EB.3's `candidates(merged, repo)` was replaced by it) + EB.5c `PathResolver::new(&cands, &renames)` (renames = EB.5c's `rename_pairs` over the repo's history snapshot under its recorded root, empty without one) and the path -> MODULE map `external::history::module_files` (pub(super) at HEAD; the 0.5.3 integrator dropped EB.3's visibility change, so THIS packet makes it pub(crate), no behaviour change); a unit index qname -> NodeId over every GOAL_UNIT and, per repo, (unit id) -> qnames for FC.18's keys; `HttpRouteMatcher::new(&merged.graphs)`; a span index per (repo, file): every located node's POSITION (start, end) line span, from one Locator pass, sorted by (start, Reverse(end)).
3. Per key type (`resolve` dispatches on `m.key`):
   - Path: `PathResolver::file(norm(text), ctx = the unit's other path mentions' dirs)` -> MODULE of that file: exact / rename -> One FACT (route `exact` / `rename`); suffix / name / context / rename-suffix -> One DERIVED; several suffix hits that context cannot narrow -> Ambiguous (route `suffix`); a Dir / Glob token -> `dir` / glob expansion -> Many DERIVED (route `dir` / `dir-suffix` / `glob`), over cap -> Unresolved `over_cap`; no hit -> Unresolved `no_file`. A ` (new)` marker never resolves a missing file (the token stays no_file; FC.9 reads pending vs done).
   - Qname: normalise `.` to `::` and strip `()`; exact qname via `merged.node_id_by_qname` -> One FACT `qname`; else the last two segments through find's `qname_suffix` tier restricted to the unit's repo: one -> One DERIVED `qname_suffix`, several -> Ambiguous; else Unresolved `no_symbol`.
   - Endpoint: `METHOD /path` through `HttpRouteMatcher::lookup` restricted to routes of the unit's repo first, then any repo: an exact-tier match -> One FACT `route_exact`; an inferred tier -> One DERIVED `route_<tier>`; several equal -> Ambiguous; none -> Unresolved `no_route`.
   - Url: `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/(issues|pull)/<n>` -> the FC.18 unit `goal:gh:<o>/<r>#<issue|pr><n>` when it exists -> One FACT `url`; any other URL -> Unresolved `url_unkeyed` (counted, never linked).

4. `enclosing(repo, file, line)`: the innermost located node of kind FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS / STRUCT / INTERFACE / ENUM / COMPONENT / SERVICE / STATE_VAR whose span contains `line`, else the file's MODULE, else None; ties by (span length, qname).
5. `ResolveStats` per key type: one / many / ambiguous / unresolved by reason, with Display `<key>=<one>/<many>/<amb>/<unres>`. Every map BTree; nothing iterates a HashMap into an output.

Confidence: FACT Strong, DERIVED Medium, HEURISTIC Weak. EVIDENCE `Evidence::emitter(goal::EMITTER_JOIN).rule(rule)` with the unit's page and the mention's line (0-based in the cell, as every EVIDENCE).
2. cited_by: each CiteCell -> `enclosing(repo, file, line)` -> an edge code node -> unit, rule `cites/<route>`, confidence from the cell's tier, EVIDENCE file / line = the citing comment. Citation-only units (FC.5a `citation_two_units`) are minted here as GOAL_UNIT nodes in the citing repo's goal graph (kind Instrument, title = the key) before their edges are drawn; the graph that holds them is the repo's goal graph (create it if FC.4 made none); each gets a UNIT cell (source Citation, page / line = the least (page, line) citing row) and a POSITION at that row.
3. Lineage: the Supersedes edges FC.4 drew (rule `supersedes`) form pairs (new -> old); apply EB.5b's class rule (a pair merges when it is the only partner on both sides, else the old REDIRECTS: the TRACES edge stays, no SAME_AS; classes capped at 6) plus FC.5a's instrument version pairs; each class -> a SAME_AS star member -> center (the least qname), emitter `goal:join`, rule `same_as::evidence_rule(RULE_ID_LINEAGE, diverged)` with diverged = the members' UnitCell digests differ. IdentityView then reads them as walk classes (FC.1's table row: DERIVED, walk).
4. Shape-rule refusals, counted in the marker and asserted zero in tests: an edge whose source is a DOC_SECTION / DOC_SPACE (rule 4: link at the row) -> refused; a unit qname without the `goal:<ns>#` shape or with ns == id (rule 1) -> refused; a route not in FC.5a's typed route list (rule 3: no text route can be minted; the list is a const) -> refused. All TRACES edges are deduped by (from, to, rule) keeping the strongest and sorted by (from qname, to qname, rule) before `cross_edges.extend`.

The invariance rule: the goal layer never moves a code answer. `MergedGraph::degree` (pick_primary's key), find's `degrees`, EA.3's FileIndex degree (EB.3's `Candidates.deg` reads it, so intent/text.rs needs no edit) and `cross_links_with` skip TRACES; find's `search` candidate scan and `answers::resolve_seed` skip GOAL_UNIT nodes (units are listed by `glia goal units`, FC.7, and `glia query`), so a unit can never become a find row or an answer's seed (pack / blast-radius / trace resolve text through them). DE.1 made an ambiguous bare mention bind the least-qname candidate at Weak: stable, but a coin flip (measured weak binds: glia 240 at 0.5.2 W1). The ruling: bind only when a recorded rule separates the candidates, with the rule as evidence; otherwise mint no edge, queue the question and report a gaps row. 'Measure at spec time how many proximity settles' becomes this packet's measured acceptance on glia.

For each rule: S = remaining candidates satisfying it; |S| == 1 -> pick it with that rule; |S| > 1 -> remaining = S, continue; |S| == 0 -> continue unchanged. End with no pick -> None. packets.title: The clarification queue's questions: `glia_engine::clarify::questions` turns what glia cannot settle (an ambiguous doc mention, a suspected_edge, a rotted rule, an unpaired client with candidate routes, a heuristic or ambiguous goal-id citation, an ambiguous goal path) into stable, located questions carrying evidence and candidate answers, each with the overlay stanza it implies; answered ones filtered
packets.area: FC - clarification (engine)
packets.rationale: §C (IN, James 2026-10-16): 'What glia cannot settle (an ambiguous bind, a suspected_edge, a rotted rule, a doc mention with two candidates, an unpaired client) becomes a queued question carrying its evidence and candidate answers; an agent works it through with a human, and the answer lands as the overlay stanza / DECISION cell it implies'. James: 'a review queue for human input clarification with an agent should work better [than] a db export'. The queue is a live query over the current graph (never an export): a question exists while its condition holds and no answer record names it. The conversation surface is repo-graph's MCP; the queue and answer format are glia's.

Tests in glia_config (accept / reject) and engine/tests/declared_cells.rs (the entry carries `by`).
1. Types: `#[derive(Serialize, Clone, Copy, ..)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum QuestionKind { DocMention, SuspectedEdge, RottedRule, UnpairedClient, GoalId, GoalPath, GoalCitation }` (+ `KINDS` in that order). `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize)] pub struct Choice { pub key: String /* c1, c2, .. */, pub label: String, pub target: Option<Located>, pub tier: &'static str, pub implies: String /* the TOML text of the stanza(s) this answer writes, empty for a record-only answer */, pub remove_gap: Option<String> /* a rotted_rule gap id the answer removes */ }`. `pub struct Question { pub id: String /* q:<16 hex> */, pub kind: QuestionKind, pub subject: Located, pub prompt: String, pub evidence: Vec<Evidence { text, file, line }>, pub choices: Vec<Choice> /* never empty; the last is always `none` (record only) */, pub gap: Option<String> /* the gaps row id this mirrors */, pub tier: &'static str, pub repo: String }`. id = `q:` + 16 hex of xxh64 over (kind, subject qname, the sorted non-none choice targets' qnames): stable across rebuilds and checkouts (content only).
2. Sources, each one fn, all over the merged graph and one Locator:
   - DocMention: each FC.11 `AmbiguousMention` -> choices per candidate implying `[[edge]]\nfrom = "<section qname>"\nto = "<candidate qname>"\ncategory = "DOCUMENTS"\norigin = "human"`; evidence = the doc line holding the span.
   - SuspectedEdge: each `suspected::suspected_rows` row -> one choice implying its `draft` stanza (CD.3b's [[edge]] text, the `# gap:` comment kept) + none.
   - RottedRule: each `rotted_rule` gaps row -> choices `remove` (remove_gap = the row id, implies empty) and none (keep it; the record says why).
   - UnpairedClient: each `unpaired_endpoint` row that has candidate routes (the `suffix_of=` / `route_prefix|edge` candidates gaps already computes: factor that code in gaps.rs into `pub(crate) fn endpoint_candidates(merged, loc, endpoint) -> Vec<(NodeId, &'static str)>` used by both) -> one choice per candidate route implying `[[edge]] from = <endpoint qname> to = <route qname> category = "HTTP_CALLS" origin = "human"` + none.
   - GoalId: every TRACES `cites/<route>` edge whose route is `recent-scope` / `newest-scope` (HEURISTIC) -> choices: the bound unit and every other GOAL_UNIT with the same id (other namespaces), each implying `[[edge]] from = <citing qname> to = <unit qname> category = "TRACES" origin = "human"`; plus every FC.4 citation counted unresolved `ambiguous` that FC.5a can still list.
   - GoalPath: every unit NamesFile mention whose FC.5a resolution is Ambiguous -> one choice per candidate MODULE implying a TRACES `[[edge]]` unit -> module.
   - GoalCitation: every Citation mention with no instrument (`how = none`) -> one choice per declared instrument implying a `[[note]]`-free record only (the fix is in the doc: the prompt says `name the instrument on the row`), plus none. (Record-only: the answer is the human's edit of the doc; the record stops the question repeating.)

Empty -> absence `no_questions` (FACT).

packets.rationale: §F item 6 (James 2026-10-16: 'it did a cache search with flow it didn't find it because it thought the flow was named cache'). trace's entry-flow fallback matches flow keys made from entry NAMES alone (engine/src/trace.rs module doc 'Keys come from names alone'), so 'cache' finds a flow named cache, never the flows that go through a cache. The fix is lexical and typed (node kinds, mechanisms, data entities, hosts, docs); the semantic tier (§B, §3 ruling 2) is the embeddings group's to add, behind item 13's gate.
entry_points: engine/src/trace.rs: `ConceptOptions`, `ConceptHit`, `ConceptTier`, `concept_flows`, `concept_flows_with_live`; `resolve` / the entry-flow tier (LD.4b) switched to the concept index
cli/src/cmd/query/flows.rs: `--concept <word>`

new files (new): engine/tests/concept_flows.rs
packets.implementation:
1. Words: `fn words(s: &str) -> Vec<String>`: split on non-alphanumerics and lower->Upper camel steps, lowercase, drop tokens < 2 chars; a query word also matches its plural / singular by a trailing `s` / `es` strip (no stemmer). A multi-word query matches a flow when EVERY query word matches somewhere in it; the row's tier is the weakest of the words' best tiers and its hop the deepest of their matching hops.
2. `#[derive(Serialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum ConceptTier { Entry, HopName, HopQname, Kind, Mechanism, DataEntity, ExternalHost, Doc }` (best first). Per flow (the EntryFlow list `entry_flows_with_live` returns: one walk, identity quotient as today), per hop node the facts: Entry = the entry's key / name words; HopName = the hop node's name words; HopQname = the qname's segment words; Kind = words of the node kind name (`CACHE` -> cache, `QUEUE_PRODUCER` -> queue, producer; `DATA_ENTITY` -> data, entity); Mechanism = words of the hop's edge category (`QUEUE_FLOWS` -> queue, flows; `ACCESSES_DATA` -> accesses, data; `HTTP_CALLS` -> http, calls); DataEntity = the names of DATA_ENTITY / DATABASE / CACHE / BLOB_STORE / SEARCH_INDEX nodes the hop node has an ACCESSES_DATA / USES edge to (one hop out, not walked); ExternalHost = the host words of an ENDPOINT the hop reaches with ORIGIN `external` (CJ.3's host); Doc = heading words of DOC_SECTIONs with a DOCUMENTS edge INTO the hop node (only a section's heading, never its body: a typed doc link, not text similarity). Facts computed once per call per node (a BTreeMap<NodeId, NodeFacts> over the flows' hop nodes).
3. `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ConceptHit { pub rank: usize, pub key: String, pub entry: Located, pub tier: ConceptTier, pub matched: Vec<String> /* query word -> what matched, `cache -> kind CACHE`, */, pub hop: Option<TraceHop> /* the matching hop (None for an Entry match) */, pub depth: usize /* the hop's depth, 0 for Entry */, pub reach: usize, pub mechanisms: Vec<&'static str> }`. `pub struct ConceptOptions { pub depth: usize /* 6 */, pub limit: usize /* 20, 0 = all */, pub collapse: Collapse }`. `pub fn concept_flows(merged, repo_labels, word, opts) -> Answer<ConceptHit>` (+ `_with_live`). Rank key: (tier, depth asc, reach desc, key asc, entry qname asc). Absence `no_match` (FACT) noting `no entry flow touches <word> by name, kind, mechanism, data entity, host or doc heading`.
4. trace: the LD.4b entry-flow tier is KEPT first, unchanged (`resolved_by = "entry_flow"`, keys from names alone, only matching entries walked); only when it matches no key does trace run `concept_flows` and seed from its top hit (`resolved_by = "concept"`, `concept_tier=<t>` in the `[trace]` marker). So every answer that resolved before resolves identically, the cost of walking every entry flow is paid only where the old answer was an absence, and the change is new answers where LD.4a / LD.4b gave `none` (declared). Update the trace.rs module doc ('Seeds' paragraph).
5. CLI flows.rs: `--concept <word>` (conflicts with `--features`, `--out`); table `| # | key | entry | tier | matched | hop | depth | location |`; `--json` the Answer envelope `{results, absence}`; exit 0 with rows, 1 on the absence. Regenerate cli/surface/flows.txt; README usage line. py/src/trace.rs: `concept_flows(word, depth=6, limit=20, collapse=True)` -> dict; surfaces regenerated.
6. Marker: `[concept] word=<w> flows=<f> hits=<h> tiers=<tier:n,..> surface=<s>`.
7. Tests (engine/tests/concept_flows.rs, a fixture: `POST /orders` handler -> OrderService.place -> a redis CACHE node via ACCESSES_DATA; `GET /health` touching nothing; a docs section `## Caching` DOCUMENTS the service): `cache` finds `post_/orders` at tier Kind with the CACHE hop and its depth; `orders cache` needs both words; `health` -> Entry; `caching` -> Doc via the heading; a word nothing touches -> absence; order deterministic; engine/tests/trace_paths.rs: a dead-end feature whose key matches resolves exactly as before (resolved_by still `entry_flow`, same seed) and `cache` on the fixture now resolves to the flow.
packets.acceptance: `cargo test -p glia-engine --test concept_flows --test trace_paths --test entry_flows` green; `cargo test --manifest-path cli/Cargo.toml flows_cli cli_surface readme_surface` green; py surface green; `bash scripts/rank-gate.sh check` prints `[rank-gate] check: ok` (trace gains a last-resort fallback; no gated ranker reads it, the check confirms); clippy -D warnings clean.

packets.rationale: §F item 15: 'A snapshots/ step ingests PR and issue title / body / linked commits through gh (never inside a build; cached; public repos for the eval)'. Review's real intent is the PR description and a task's is its issue (round 1 measured commit subjects only). The snapshot is an external input like history sync: the snapshots crate is the only glia code that spawns a process, and only when a sync is called.

1. code-domain/src/snapshots.rs (beside the history snapshot types): `pub const GH_SNAPSHOT_DIR: &str = "gh-snapshot"; pub const GH_VERSION: u32 = 1;` `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct GhPr { pub n: u64, pub title: String /* SUBJECT_CAP */, #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = String::is_empty)] pub body: String /* MESSAGE_BODY_CAP, redacted */, pub merged_at: String /* RFC 3339 */, #[serde(default)] pub merge_sha: Option, #[serde(default)] pub commits: Vec /* shas */, #[serde(default)] pub files: Vec /* repo-relative, sorted, <= 300 */, #[serde(default)] pub closes: Vec /* sorted */ }`, `pub struct GhIssue { pub n: u64, pub title, pub body, pub state: String /* open|closed */, #[serde(default)] pub closed_at: Option, #[serde(default)] pub labels: Vec }`, `pub struct GhMeta { pub version: u32, pub repo: String /* owner/name */, pub fetched_at: String, pub prs: usize, pub issues: usize, pub data_hash: String }`, `pub struct GhSnapshot { pub meta, pub prs: Vec /* by n */, pub issues: Vec /* by n */ }`; `pub fn write_gh(root, &GhSnapshot) -> Result<(), String>` (prs.jsonl, issues.jsonl with `write_atomic`, meta.json LAST, data_hash over the two files like the history snapshot's `data_hash`); `pub fn gh_prs_from_json(text: &str) -> Result, String>` / `gh_issues_from_json(text)` (the `gh ... --json` DTOs parsed HERE, where serde_json already is: glia-snapshots has no serde_json dependency and adding one is a Cargo.lock edit; the DTO keeps only `oid` from each commit and drops every author / login / email field, so no identity reaches the snapshot); `write_gh` also writes `gh-snapshot/.gitignore` = `*` (the dir ignores itself, as scip-snapshot does: a repo whose `.glia/.gitignore` predates this line never gets it, and PR text of a private repo must never be committed); `pub fn read_gh(root) -> Option` (None silently when absent; a version / hash mismatch -> None plus one `[gh] snapshot rejected dir= reason=` line); every title / body read back passes `redact_untrusted` again. 2. snapshots/src/gh.rs: `pub struct GhOptions { pub repo: Option /* owner/name; default from the origin remote */, pub prs: usize /* 500 */, pub issues: usize /* 500 */, pub gh: String /* "gh" */ }` (Default) and `pub fn gh_sync(repo_path: &Path, opts: &GhOptions) -> Result`: slug = opts.repo, else `git remote get-url origin` parsed for `github.com[:/]/(.git)?` (Err `not a GitHub remote; pass --repo owner/name`); `gh --version` (Err `gh not found: install the GitHub CLI`); `gh pr list --repo --state merged --limit --json number,title,body,mergedAt,mergeCommit,commits,files,closingIssuesReferences` and `gh issue list --repo --state all --limit --json number,title,body,state,closedAt,labels` through a private `run_gh(args)` mirroring git_history.rs's `run_git` hygiene (argv only, no shell, stdin null, env GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1, GH_PAGER=cat, NO_COLOR=1; stderr captured into the Err); parse through code-domain's `gh_prs_from_json` / `gh_issues_from_json`; title / body through `redact_untrusted` (counted), capped; files sorted and capped; then MERGE with an existing snapshot (`read_gh`): rows keyed by number, a fetched row replaces the stored one, stored rows not fetched are kept (the cache: a later sync with a smaller limit keeps history); write. No token or user name is stored; the GitHub CLI uses the caller's auth. `GhSummary { repo, prs, issues, fetched_prs, fetched_issues, redacted, kept }`. 3. snapshots/src/lib.rs: the module doc's list gains `[gh_sync]` (spawns `gh` and `git remote`, only when called); `.glia/.gitignore`'s GLIA_GITIGNORE gains `gh-snapshot/`. 4. Marker: `[gh] sync repo= prs=

(fetched=) issues= (fetched=) redacted= kept= surface=`. 5. Tests (snapshots/tests/gh.rs): `gh` is never run in tests: `GhOptions.gh` points at a test script under the crate's tests dir printing canned JSON for each argv (written to a temp dir at test start, chmod +x; skip on non-unix with a cfg); the sync writes the three files; a body holding a fake token pattern is redacted; a second sync with a smaller limit keeps the older rows; read_gh round-trips; a corrupted prs.jsonl is rejected with the marker; a non-GitHub remote errs.

packets.area: FC - PR / issue intent (experiment)
packets.rationale: §F item 15: 'rank_eval compares PR text vs subject on the gate repos. If PR text wins, review reads it (--pr <n>), in a follow-up wave of this leap.' Round 1 found the subject alone keeps 89-106% of the gain on six repos; whether the PR body adds more (or dilutes, as task rows as BM25 text did, scoreboard row 2) is unmeasured. Measure first, build only on PASS (the spec rule for a measured experiment).

packets.implementation:
1. Data: for each public rank-gate snapshot with PRs (pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples; glia has no PRs: James pushes directly, so it is not a PR repo), run `glia gh sync <clone> --repo <owner/name> --prs 2000 --issues 2000` once and copy prs.jsonl / issues.jsonl into bench/pr-intent/<label>/ (public data; bodies already redacted). README.md records the commands, the date and the counts.
2. rank_eval `--pr-intent <dir>`: load `<dir>/<label>/prs.jsonl` (+ issues) with serde (code-domain's GhPr / GhIssue). A test commit is PR-MATCHED when its sha is a PR's `merge_sha` (squash / merge commit) or the LAST of a PR's `commits` (rebase merge); the PR-matched set is the subset of the existing round-3 review-shape queries (k2 / k3 / half, rank_eval's eligibility and leak-free prefix unchanged). Intent variants per query: S = the commit subject (today), P = the PR title, PB = title + `\n` + body, PBI = PB + each closed issue's title + body, and the CONTROL Xperm = the PB text of ANOTHER PR-matched query of the same repo (a seeded derangement over the PR-matched queries in commit order, `--seed`), so generic PR prose (templates, checklists, boilerplate) is measured apart from the PR's own content. Rankers rerun per variant: T1s, H9s50, LX[IDR,H9s50] (IDR over the variant's text: EB.6's route), and SELt2's online pick (the selection replay with the variant as each test commit's title, so the pick is per variant). Leak-free: a PR whose `merged_at` is after the test commit is never used for an earlier query (only its own query's text).
3. Output: per (repo, shape, ranker) recall@10 / MRR for S / P / PB / PBI, the paired differences P - S, PB - S, PBI - S with the commit-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (rank_eval's `--boot`), coverage (PR-matched queries / all queries), into `--r3md`-style markdown via `--pr-md <file>`.
4. PASS rule (stated in the report before the numbers): a variant V in {P, PB, PBI} PASSES when, for SELt2's pick on the k2 shape, V - S recall@10 has CI > 0 on at least 2 of the 3 repos AND V - Xperm recall@10 has CI > 0 on those same repos (the gain is the PR's own text, not PR-shaped prose) AND V - S is not significantly negative (CI wholly < 0) on any repo or shape; the report names the best passing variant (largest mean V - S), else `FAIL`. With fewer than 30 PR-matched queries on a repo, that repo is `thin` and counts as neither (and if two are thin the report says the test is underpowered: FAIL, with the counts).
5. The report dev-notes/pr-intent-eval-<date>.md: the rule, the tables, the verdict line `PR intent: PASS (<variant>)` or `PR intent: FAIL (<reason>)`, aggregate numbers only.

packets.rationale: §F item 14: 'The rankings can only name existing files: 128 of 222 files of the law-driven change were new; co-change is cold for 33-49% of seeds. Score, on held-out commits that add files, the directory a new file lands in and the sibling it was patterned on (structure, co-change, intent, calibration as in 0.5.3), against controls. If a ranker beats them on the gate repos, it ships as an answer in a follow-up wave of this leap; if not, the report closes it.'

packets.implementation:
1. Query set: rank_eval's leak-free test commits (eligibility unchanged) that ADD at least one candidate-extension file (`git log --name-status --no-renames` A rows; renames are not additions); seeds = the commit's MODIFIED candidate files (k1 / k2 / half shapes over them; a commit with no modified file uses the find shape: intent text only); intent = the subject. Truth: DIR = the directories of the added files; SIB = per added file, the file of the parent revision with the highest line-set Jaccard to the new file's content (trimmed non-empty lines, `git show`), ties to the same directory then path; no sibling when the best Jaccard < 0.2 (counted).
2. Directory rankers, each a score per directory of the parent revision's candidate files, where a file's score counts toward its IMMEDIATE directory only (summing every level to the root would put the root and `src/` above every leaf by construction, so hit@k would measure depth, not placement); a truth file whose directory did not exist in the parent revision is scored on its nearest existing ancestor and the query is counted `new_dir` (reported separately, and in the pooled numbers): Dstr = sum of P1 / PT* file scores (rank_eval run_query) per directory; Dco = sum of C0 per directory; Dtxt = sum of T1s per directory; Dmm = mm-blend of the three (rank_eval's minmax helper); Dsel = the online pick among {Dstr, Dco, Dtxt, Dmm} by r3_select's prequential rule (EC.3's replay logic). Controls: Cseed = the seeds' directories by seed count, then depth desc; Cpop = directories by candidate file count; Crand = a seeded random order. Sibling rankers: the top-3 directories' files ordered by the same scores, plus control Csib = the most recently modified file in the seeds' directory.
3. Metrics: dir hit@1 / hit@3 (any truth directory in the top k, exact match on the immediate directory, the `new_dir` ancestor rule above), sibling recall@5, per (repo, shape), with the commit-cluster bootstrap CI of each ranker minus the best control (Cseed unless Cpop is better on that repo).
4. PASS rule (in the report before the numbers): the directory answer PASSES when one non-control ranker R (the same R on every repo) beats the best control on dir hit@3 with CI > 0 on at least 3 of the 4 public gate repos (glia's pinned v0.5.2 snapshot, pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples) and is not significantly below it on any; the sibling answer PASSES under the same rule on sibling recall@5 against Csib. A repo with < 30 added-file queries is `thin` (neither). The verdict line: `Placement: PASS (<ranker>[, sibling])` / `Placement: FAIL (<reason>)`.
5. The report dev-notes/place-eval-<date>.md: rule, coverage (queries with additions / all), tables, verdict; the four public gate repos only (the rank gate's public rule: no `--private` run feeds the report).

packets.implementation:
All new files are (new) except engine/src/why.rs.
1. why.rs: add `pub fn edge_tier` (doc: the reading `why`, `check` and `glia query` share; the precision audit samples by it). No other change.
2. edge_audit.rs `sample`: `generate_one(repo)` (GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 set by the script), a Locator over the merged graph. Population = every edge of every RepoGraph plus merged.cross_edges whose `from` and `to` are both located OR whose evidence names a file (an edge with neither cannot be judged against source: counted per stratum as `unjudgeable` and reported, never sampled), minus edges whose from-node file starts with a `--skip` prefix. Stratum = (category name, tier word from `why::edge_tier`). Per stratum target n = floors.n_per_stratum (n_structural for the structural list). POOLING across repos happens in `report`, so `sample` writes each repo's FULL stratum sizes and a per-repo sample of min(N_h, n): the plan's n is split across repos proportionally to N_h with every repo holding the stratum getting at least 1 (largest-remainder rounding, ties by label) - so `sample` takes all four snapshots in one invocation (`--repo` repeatable, paired with `--label`/`--rev`). Selection is deterministic: key = xxh64(seed || label || category || from qname || to qname || evidence rule || evidence file || evidence line) (twox-hash, already an engine dependency), take the n smallest keys; NO HashMap iteration reaches the output (collect into Vec, sort by key). Sample row (one JSON object per line, sorted by (category, tier, key)): {id: 16-hex key, label, rev, category, tier, tier_note, emitter, rule, site:{file,line(1-based)}, from:{qname,kind,file,line}, to:{qname,kind,file,line}}. No source text is written (public-repo licences; `show` reads the snapshot). Header line 0 per label: {"stratum_sizes": {"<cat>|<tier>": N_h, ..}, "unjudgeable": {..}, "edges": E} so report knows population sizes. Marker per repo: `[edge-audit] sample label=<l> edges=<E> strata=<s> sampled=<n> unjudgeable=<u> seed=<seed>`.
3. `show`: for each sample, print the header line `<id> <category> <tier> <from qname> -> <to qname>` then the evidence site excerpt (+-4 lines, the site line marked `>`) and the target definition excerpt (+-2 lines) from `--root` (the snapshot copy), so a judge works from source.
4. `report`: read every samples file and every verdict file (rows {id, verdict: correct|wrong|unsure, reason, judge}). Per pooled stratum h: N_h (sum over repos), n_h judged (unsure excluded and counted), p_h = correct / (correct + wrong), Wilson 95% interval (z = 1.959964). Per category and per tier: the stratified estimate p = sum(W_h p_h) with W_h = N_h / N and variance sum(W_h^2 p_h(1-p_h)/n_h (1 - n_h/N_h)), interval p +- 1.96 sqrt(var) clipped to [0,1] (a stratum with n_h = N_h has zero variance: census). Per repo the same table restricted to that repo's samples (reported, not gated). A stratum is UNDER FLOOR when p_h < floors[tier]; INSUFFICIENT when n_h < 10 after unsure; NOISY when unsure > 10% of its judged rows. report.json: {floors, strata:[{category,tier,N,n,correct,wrong,unsure,p,lo,hi,status}], categories:[..], tiers:[..], repos:{..}, under_floor:["<cat>|<tier>"..]} sorted by (category, tier); report.md renders the same as tables plus a short method section. `--check` recomputes from the committed samples + verdicts and exits 1 when report.json differs byte-for-byte (the report is derived, never hand-edited). Marker: `[edge-audit] report strata=<s> judged=<j> unsure=<u> under_floor=<k> insufficient=<i>`. A verdict row whose id is in no samples file, or a sample with two verdicts from the same judge, is an error (exit 2) naming the id.
5. scripts/edge-audit.sh (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, the rank-gate.sh style): `sample` runs `bash scripts/rank-gate.sh fetch`, makes `$DIR/glia@<rev12>/` with `git archive HEAD | tar -x` (a `.complete` marker), builds the example in release, runs one `sample` over the four trees, writes bench/edge-audit/samples/audit.jsonl; refuses a snapshots row that is not `public` except the glia row (the repo itself, public). `show <label>` and `report` wrap the example. `unset GLIA_RANK_PRIVATE` first; never passes `--private`.
6. Unit tests inside the example (`cargo test -p glia-engine --example edge_audit`): Wilson interval values (p=27/30 gives [0.744, 0.965] to 3 dp), the stratified variance with a census stratum, proportional allocation with the at-least-one rule, and determinism (two `sample` runs on one tree write identical bytes). INTEGRATOR (audit the pre-0.5.4-layer vocabulary): the sampler's population also excludes every TRACES edge, every edge touching a GOAL_UNIT node and every edge whose EVIDENCE emitter is resolver:org_packages (FA.22 / FA.23): those layers land concurrently in 0.5.4's first waves and are gated by their own audits (FC.6's goal_audit, FA.22 / FA.23's fixtures); `excluded` counts per reason go in the sample header and the marker (`excluded=<n>`). This keeps the audit 0.5.5's baseline of the 0.5.3 edge vocabulary whatever lands before FD.3a samples.

(2) `bash scripts/edge-audit.sh sample` twice on the same HEAD writes byte-identical bench/edge-audit/samples/audit.jsonl and prints four `[edge-audit] sample label=` lines (glia, shell, websocket, samples) with strata > 0; record edges / strata / sampled per label and wall time in the commit body. packets.rationale: Seed §F item 2: 'every needle scanner reads through the CJ.1 code guard (cron YAML, CLI INVOCATION_PATTERNS, ...)'. `)

packets.title: TypeScript: interface members are METHOD nodes (`method_signature`, and a `property_signature` whose type is a function type) recorded in `interface_methods`, so an interface-typed receiver binds its CALLS (A6.6) and implementations pair through method-level IMPLEMENTS
packets.area: FD per-language residuals: TypeScript (seed §D)
packets.rationale: Seed §D: 'TS interface members are not METHOD nodes, so interface-typed receivers bind nothing.' Re-verified at HEAD 37fb9384: `export interface Store { load(id: string): string; }` and `function run(s: Store) { s.load("x"); }` produce no edge from run. The machinery exists for other languages: graph/src/types.rs `symbols.interface_methods` (A6.6), graph/src/calls.rs reads it for an INTERFACE-typed receiver ('binds the interface's own METHOD through interface_methods (A6.6); the implementation is one method-level IMPLEMENTS hop further (emit_method_level_implements)'), and PHP / Go / Java mint interface METHODs. The TS parser's `visit_interface` (parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs) mints the INTERFACE only; class `method_signature` is deliberately ignored ('the implementation after it'), which is right for overload signatures in a class but leaves interfaces with no members.
entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - visit_interface: for each `method_signature` child of the interface body, and each `property_signature` whose type annotation is a `function_type`, mint a METHOD `<iface qname>::<name>` (POSITION at the member, CODE the member text) as a child of the INTERFACE (nav parent = interface), recorded where the graph build fills `interface_methods` (read how PHP does it: parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs comment 'children of it, so A6.6 can pair an implementation with them'); an overload set (two signatures of one name) mints one METHOD at the first

packets.rationale: §E W2 (DH.20): 'a client call with a trailing closure mints a phantom `POST /https://...` ROUTE; `app.get("/users")` reads `GET //users`; `app.get(use: index)` mints no `GET /`; grouped builders (`app.grouped("users")`) do not join the prefix'. Re-verified at HEAD 37fb9384 on a probe package: ROUTE `GET //users` and ROUTE `POST /https://api.example.com/x` (from `client.post("https://api.example.com/x") { req in }` inside a function, not a router). These are false nodes on any Vapor server.
entry_points: parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs - the Vapor route reader (DH.20's `use:` / trailing-closure rule): path components joined with single `/` (a component that already starts with `/` is not prefixed again); the receiver must be a route builder (`app`, `routes`, a `RoutesBuilder`-typed parameter, or a var assigned from `.grouped(` / `.group(` of one), never a `Client` / `req.client` / an `http` client; a first argument that is a URL with a scheme (`http://`, `https://`) is never a route path
parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs - `app.get(use: handler)` with no path components mints `GET /`

parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs - `let users = app.grouped("users")` then `users.get(":id", use: show)` mints `GET /users/:id` (one level of grouped var in the same function; `app.group("x") { r in r.get(..) }` closure form too)

packets.rationale: Seed §E W11 (DB.4, DB.3b): 'a `[[constraint]] rule` with no `violation` output predicate is a `glia check` error (exit 2) but no `rotted_rule` gaps row, because the row reads `rules::validate`, which has no output-predicate check'; W11 (DB.3b): 'each transitive forbid rule re-tiers every kept edge of its chain (`edge_tier_of` -> `Evidence::of`); several transitive rules over one big merge could share one per-edge level vector on Ctx, keyed by edge ordinal'; W13 (DB.8b): '`reflexion::derive` runs unbudgeted (`max_rows = usize::MAX`); a finite budget must exceed |placed nodes| x |declared paths| bindings for `owns`' (HEAD: reflexion.rs `options.max_rows = usize::MAX`); W14 (DZ.2): 'the header comment of engine/src/rules/reflexion.dl still calls the native functions the parity oracle "until DB.8b deletes them"' (HEAD line 3).

engine/src/gaps.rs - rotted_rule reads validate_constraint
engine/src/rules/reflexion.rs - max_rows = (placed nodes x declared paths) x 4 + 10,000, computed per call; a Budget error is a check error naming reflexion
engine/src/check.rs - Ctx gains a lazily built `edge_levels: Vec<u8>` keyed by edge ordinal, read by every transitive forbid instead of re-tiering
engine/src/rules/reflexion.dl - header comment: the goldens are the oracle
markers: `[gaps] rotted_rule no_violation=<n>`; `[rules] budget pred=reflexion rows=<n> cap=<c>` (existing format) when hit; `[check] transitive edge_levels=<e> rules=<r>`

packets.implementation:
Every bench/agent-ab file is (new); stdlib Python 3.11 only (json, subprocess, hashlib, re, argparse, pathlib, tempfile).
1. repos.json: six rows. shell / websocket / samples take `gate_rev` from bench/rank-gate/snapshots.json (EG.3) and `end_rev` = the upstream default branch tip at task-build time (`git ls-remote <url> HEAD`, expanded to 40 hex and recorded); commons-text (https://github.com/apache/commons-text.git), microservices-demo (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo.git), click (https://github.com/pallets/click.git) have `gate_rev: null` and `tuned: false` (shell / websocket / samples `tuned: true`). `public: true` on every row; tasks.py refuses a row without it or with a non-https url.
2. Cache: DIR=${GLIA_AGENT_AB_DIR:-$HOME/.cache/glia-agent-ab}; `$DIR/<label>.git` bare clone (`git clone --bare --quiet`), fetched only when `git cat-file -e <end_rev>^{commit}` fails. Nothing is written inside the glia tree except tasks/*.jsonl. .gitignore gains `bench/agent-ab/.cache/` (a guard should someone point DIR there).
3. Eligibility over `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges <end_rev>` (newest first), per commit C with parent P (`C^1`): (a) author / committer not a bot (`[bot]`, dependabot, renovate, github-actions); (b) subject after stripping a conventional-commit prefix (`^[a-z]+(\([^)]*\))?!?: `) has >= 4 words and does not match `^(bump|release|merge|revert|update dependenc|upgrade dependenc|format|lint|typo|changelog|docs?\b|v?\d+\.\d+)` (case-insensitive); (c) `git diff -M --numstat --name-status P C` code files (extension in CODE_EXTS, a module constant: .go .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .py .java .kt .dart .rs .cs .rb .php .swift .c .cc .cpp .h .hpp .scala .ex .exs .proto .sol .vue): 1..=6 NON-TEST code files changed, at least one of them modified (not only added / deleted), total added+deleted lines over code files 5..=300, renames (R status) <= half of the files; (d) a test file is classified by TEST_RES (path has a `test`/`tests`/`__tests__`/`testdata` directory component, or the basename matches `_test\.go$`, `^test_.*\.py$`, `_test\.py$`, `Test.*\.java$`, `.*Test\.java$`, `_test\.dart$`, `\.(spec|test)\.[jt]sx?$`); (e) not already selected; (f) merge-based histories (pallets/click and the apache repos merge PRs with merge commits, so first-parent non-merge commits alone are too few): a first-parent merge commit M whose message is GitHub's `Merge pull request #<n> from <branch>` with a non-empty title line is one candidate over `git diff M^1 M` (the PR's whole change, rules (a)-(d) applied to it), commit = M, parent = M^1, prompt_subject = the title line, `pr: <n>` recorded; the PR body is never fetched (it states the solution) and `#<n>` of a merge is never treated as an issue. Take the newest N (default 10) eligible per repo. Deterministic: the same end_rev and rules give the same rows (test 4).
4. Issue text (a snapshot step at task-build time, never during a run): when the subject or body names `#<n>` / `fixes|closes|resolves #<n>` and the repo is on github.com, fetch `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq '{title,body,pull_request}'`; keep it only when it is an issue (no `pull_request` key) with a non-empty title; body truncated at 4,000 chars on a line boundary. No `gh` or no network: the row keeps `issue: null` and `issue_fetch: "unavailable"`, never fails the build. The commit BODY is never kept as prompt text (it often states the solution).
5. Row schema (one JSON object per line, keys sorted): {id: "<label>-<C[:12]>", repo, commit: C, parent: P, author_time (unix), subject (raw), prompt_subject (prefix-stripped), issue: {number, title, body}|null, issue_fetch: "ok"|"none"|"unavailable", after_gate_rev: bool (C is a descendant of gate_rev, i.e. unseen by 0.5.3's tuning; null when gate_rev is null), truth: {code: [{path, status (A|M|D|R), old_path|null, hunks: [[start, len], ..] in PARENT coordinates from `git diff -U0 P C -- <path>` (`@@ -s,l` pairs; l=0 means a pure insertion at s)}], tests: [paths], other: [paths]}, stats: {code_files, code_lines, test_files}}. Rows sorted newest first, as selected.
6. `tasks.py check`: re-derives every row of every committed file from the bare clones (same end_rev, same rules; it never refetches issue text: the committed `issue` / `issue_fetch` fields are carried over, so `check` runs offline) and exits 1 naming each differing id; prints `[agent-ab] tasks repo=<label> rows=<n> issues=<k> after_gate=<g> sha256=<first 12 of the file's sha256>` per repo and `[agent-ab] tasks total=<n> repos=<r>`.
7. README.md: sections What it measures, Arms (FE.2), Tasks (rules above, why glia is excluded), Running (FE.2 / FE.3 commands), Cost (FE.2's estimate, the pilot gate), Reproducibility (what is pinned and what cannot be: the model's sampling), The 0.5.5 baseline (FE.4's baseline.json).
8. test_tasks.py (`python3 test_tasks.py`, pytest-collectable like bench/substrate-gap/test_run.py): builds a throwaway git repo in a tempdir with scripted commits (a 2-file fix, a bot commit, a 9-file refactor, a docs-only commit, a test-only commit, a rename-heavy commit, a fix whose subject has 3 words, and a `Merge pull request #7 from x/y` merge of a 2-file branch) and asserts exactly the fix and the merge (as one task over M^1..M, prompt_subject = its title line) are selected with the expected hunks and statuses, the issue path is skipped offline (`GLIA_AGENT_AB_OFFLINE=1`), and two builds are byte-identical.

No new crate or dependency (no F0 needed).

packets.implementation:
All (new) except README.md (FE.1's). Stdlib Python only. DIR as FE.1.
1. config.json defaults: model `claude-opus-5-5` (James may change it, open question), claude_version = the `claude --version` string at implementation time, runs 3, max_turns 40, timeout_s 1200, max_usd 400, disallowed_tools ["Agent","Task","WebFetch","WebSearch","NotebookEdit"], glia_threads 4. g053.rev: `v0.5.3` when that tag exists, else the commit recorded in config as `rev` by hand (0.5.3's last close-out / EZ.2 commit) - run.py refuses a rev that `git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}` cannot resolve.
2. prompt.txt (fixed text, `{repo}`, `{task}` substituted): 'You are working in a checkout of the {repo} repository. Make this change:\n\n{task}\n\nEdit the files that need to change. Do not commit, push, or reformat unrelated code, and do not run the full test suite. When you are done, reply with the list of files you changed.' {task} = prompt_subject, plus '\n\nIssue #<n>: <title>\n<body>' when issue is set. Identical for every arm.
3. `run.py binaries`: per glia arm, `git worktree add --detach $DIR/glia@<sha12> <rev>` from this repo (reused when present), `cargo build --release -p glia-cli` there (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$DIR/target@<sha12>), copy target/release/glia to `$DIR/bin/<arm>/glia`, then delete `$DIR/target@<sha12>` and `git worktree remove` the checkout (a release target is tens of GB; the binary and meta.json are all a later run needs; a present `$DIR/bin/<arm>/glia` whose meta.json sha matches skips the build), write `$DIR/bin/<arm>/meta.json` {rev, sha, version: `glia --version` output}, and `git show <rev>:skills/glia/SKILL.md` to `$DIR/skills/<arm>/glia/SKILL.md`. Prints `[agent-ab] binary arm=<a> sha=<12> version=<v>`.
4. Per session checkout (leak-free: the copy holds no commit after the parent): `git -C $DIR/<label>.git config uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant true`; `git init -q <copy>`; `git -C <copy> fetch -q $DIR/<label>.git <parent>`; `git -C <copy> checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD`; `git -C <copy> branch -q -f main FETCH_HEAD && git -C <copy> checkout -q main` (history sync reads HEAD); `.git/info/exclude` gains `.glia/` and `.claude/`. Copy path `$DIR/work/<run_id>/<task_id>/<arm>/<rep>/` (deleted after scoring unless `--keep`). Before the session, assert `git -C <copy> cat-file -e <commit>` FAILS (the task commit is absent), else abort the run.
5. Glia prep for a glia arm, timed and recorded as `prep_ms`, never on the agent's clock: `glia build <copy>`, `glia history sync <copy>`, and for g053 also `glia history calibrate <copy>` (EC.6); a non-zero exit marks the session `prep_failed` (scored as missing, reported). The arm's skill copied to `<copy>/.claude/skills/glia/SKILL.md`.
6. Environment, identical for every arm except PATH's first entry: (a) a fresh Claude Code config per run: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$DIR/claude-config/<run_id>` (created empty; no user CLAUDE.md, no user skills, plugins, hooks or auto-memory can reach a session: the user's own ~/.claude carries glia / repo-graph instructions and context-injecting hooks that would contaminate the control); auth only from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (metered) or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (`claude setup-token`, subscription) in the caller's env - run.py refuses to start when neither is set and records which (`auth: api_key|oauth_token`, never the value); (b) PATH = `$DIR/bin/deny` (shims named `glia`, `mcp-repo-graph` and `repo-graph` that print `<name>: command not found` to stderr and exit 127) then os.environ PATH, with glia arms putting `$DIR/bin/<arm>` before the deny dir; nothing else is removed from PATH, so every arm keeps the same git / grep / language tools; (c) GLIA_THREADS from config, GLIA_RANK_PRIVATE unset.
7. Session command (cwd = copy): `claude -p <prompt> --model <model> --output-format stream-json --verbose --mcp-config bench/agent-ab/empty-mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources project --permission-mode bypassPermissions --max-turns <n> --disallowedTools <each>`; stdout streamed to `$DIR/sessions/<run_id>/<task_id>/<arm>/<rep>.jsonl`; killed after timeout_s (terminated=`timeout`). Rate limits: the repo-graph bench rule (a result whose error text reads as a rate limit sleeps until its reset, else 900 s, max 6 h, up to 5 attempts).
8. Isolation (`run.py isolation`, and checked on EVERY session from its stream's first `system`/`init` event): mcp_servers empty; the init event's tool list holds no `mcp__` tool and none of the disallowed tools; the skill names it lists (the field the pinned Claude Code version emits - record which in README) contain `glia` in glia arms and no `glia*` skill in the control. A violating session is `contaminated`, excluded from scoring and reported. The transcript is also checked after the session: (i) in the control, any Bash command whose command word (after `VAR=v` prefixes / `cd x &&`) is `glia`, `mcp-repo-graph`, `repo-graph`, an absolute path ending `/glia`, or `uvx`/`pipx`/`pip` naming glia-cli / glia-py / mcp-repo-graph makes it `contaminated`; (ii) in a glia arm, a glia invocation that is not the bare `glia` on PATH (an absolute path to another binary, `uvx --from glia-cli ..`, `cargo run`) makes it `contaminated`; (iii) in every arm, a Bash command that reaches the network for the repo's history (`git clone|fetch|pull|ls-remote|remote add`, `gh `, `curl`, `wget`, or a WebFetch / WebSearch call despite the deny list) makes it `network`, excluded and reported (the leak-free checkout cannot stop the agent fetching the answer upstream). `run.py isolation` runs one cheap session per arm (`--max-turns 1`, prompt 'Reply with the word ok.') and prints `[agent-ab] isolation arm=<a> mcp=0 skills=<list> ok|FAIL`.
9. Per session, append one row to `$DIR/runs/<run_id>/sessions.jsonl` (resume skips keys already present): {run_id, task_id, repo, arm, rep, model (init event), claude_version, glia_sha|null, prep_ms, terminated (end|max_turns|timeout|error|prep_failed|contaminated|network), auth, num_turns, duration_ms, wall_ms, usage {input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens}, total_cost_usd, tool_calls {name: count}, glia_calls [{subcommand, flags}] (Bash commands whose first word after `VAR=v` prefixes / `cd x &&` is `glia`, split on `|`, `&&`, `;`), files_opened [repo-relative paths, first-open order]: Read tool `file_path`s plus Bash `cat|head|tail|less|bat|sed -n` arguments that name a file inside the copy (paths outside or under .glia/.claude are dropped), grep_calls (Grep tool + Bash rg/grep), patch: `git -C <copy> add -A -N . && git -C <copy> diff --no-color -U0 HEAD` written to `$DIR/patches/<run_id>/<key>.diff` with its sha256}.
10. Order: for rep in 1..R, for task in file order, arms in an order rotated by the task index (none,g052,g053 / g052,g053,none / ..), so time-of-day drift spreads over arms. Budget: the running sum of total_cost_usd; when it would pass max_usd the run stops cleanly (`[agent-ab] budget stop spent=<usd>`), resumable. `run.py pilot` = the first task of each repo x every arm x 1 rep, then prints `[agent-ab] pilot sessions=<n> usd=<sum> median_usd=<m> est_full_usd=<median x tasks x arms x runs> est_hours=<median wall x sessions>` and stops (the full run needs `run.py run --run-id <id>` after James approves the estimate). `run.py status` prints counts by arm / terminated.
11. test_run.py: a fake `claude` script (written to a temp bin dir) that emits a canned stream-json (init event with/without an mcp tool, a Read, a Bash `glia find . X --json`, an Edit that changes a file, a result event with usage and cost) and a fake `glia`; asserts the checkout lacks the task commit, the deny shims (control `glia` exits 127), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to an empty per-run dir and the refusal without an auth env var, control `uvx --from glia-cli glia` and glia-arm absolute-path invocations flagged `contaminated`, a `git fetch` / `curl` session flagged `network`, the metrics row (files_opened order, glia_calls, patch), contamination detection, budget stop, resume, and arm rotation. `python3 test_run.py` exit 0.
12. README.md: the Running and Cost sections. Cost, from repo-graph's bench (Sonnet 5 orientation sessions $0.09-0.68 metered) scaled to edit tasks: roughly $0.5-2 per session on Opus 5.5; full matrix 60 tasks x 3 arms x 3 runs = 540 sessions, about $300-1,000 metered (Sonnet 5.5 about half); on a Claude subscription (`apiKeySource: none`) no metered charge, but about 540 x 3-5 min of sessions against the 5-hour / weekly limits (check ~/.claude/rate-limits.json and dev-notes/wave-runner/usage_gate.py before starting). The pilot (18 sessions) measures the real figure first.

Both scripts (new); stdlib only.
1. Per session (reads FE.2's sessions.jsonl, the patch files and FE.1's task row): T = truth.code paths (for R, the new path; for D, the old path); E = non-test code files the patch touches (same CODE_EXTS / TEST_RES as tasks.py, imported from it), excluding .glia/ and .claude/. file_recall = |E n T| / |T|; file_precision = |E n T| / |E| (0 when E is empty); solved = (T subset of E) and |E \ T| <= max(2, |T|); line_overlap = over truth hunks of M files, the fraction whose parent range [s, s+max(l,1)) intersects some agent hunk's parent range widened by 3 lines on each side (agent hunks from the patch's `@@ -s,l` headers); first_truth_open = 1-based index in files_opened of the first T path, or null; opened = len(files_opened); tokens_in = input + cache_creation + cache_read; tokens_out; usd = total_cost_usd; turns; wall_s; glia_calls. Sessions terminated contaminated / network / prep_failed / error are excluded and counted; timeout / max_turns are scored as they stand (their patch is what the agent left).
1b. `--out-sessions <f>` writes the per-session metric rows of step 1 (keys sorted, sorted by (task_id, arm, rep); no paths outside the task repo, no transcript text, no patch text, only each patch's sha256), and `--from-metrics <f>` scores from such a file instead of $DIR (it needs neither transcripts nor patches), so a committed metrics file reproduces the committed baseline byte for byte.
2. Per (repo, arm, task): the mean over reps of each metric (solved as a rate). Per (repo, arm): the mean over tasks. Pooled: the mean over all tasks (each task weight 1).
3. Pairs: g052-none, g053-none, g053-g052. For each metric, the paired per-task difference of task means, and a task-cluster bootstrap (resample tasks with replacement, 2,000 resamples, `random.Random(20261023)`) 95% percentile CI, per repo and pooled; also split by after_gate_rev where a side has >= 5 tasks, and always by `tuned` (FE.1's repos.json: the untuned subset is commons-text / microservices-demo / click). Verdict per (pair, metric): `better` / `worse` when the CI excludes 0 in the metric's good direction (higher: solved, file_recall, file_precision, line_overlap; lower: opened, first_truth_open, tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, turns, wall_s), else `n.s.`.
4. The report's stated reading rule (written into the md, decided now, not after the numbers): glia (an arm) HELPS an agent when, pooled, solved or file_recall is `better` and no quality metric (solved, file_recall, line_overlap) is `worse`; or when every quality metric is `n.s.` and tokens_in or usd is `better`. It HURTS when a quality metric is `worse`. Otherwise NO MEASURED EFFECT. The 0.5.3-vs-0.5.2 line uses the same rule on g053-g052 and is what informs 0.5.4's ranking work; it is stated pooled AND on the untuned subset, and where the two disagree the report says the pooled effect rests on the repos 0.5.3 was tuned on.
5. Markdown (`--out-md`): header (date, run_id, model, claude_version, glia shas, tasks sha256 per file, sessions scored / excluded by reason); pooled table (arm x metric, mean and per-pair differences with CI and verdict); per-repo tables; a cost table (sum and median usd, tokens, wall per arm); glia usage (share of glia-arm sessions with >= 1 glia call, the subcommand histogram); the reading rule and its outcome per pair. Deterministic: rows sorted by (repo, arm), floats at 3 decimals; two runs over the same inputs are byte-identical.
6. baseline.json (`--out-json`): {schema: 1, run_id, fingerprints: {model, claude_version, glia: {arm: sha}, tasks: {file: sha256}, prompt_sha256, config_sha256}, per_task: [{task_id, arm, n, metrics}], pooled: {arm: metrics}, pairs: {pair: {metric: {diff, lo, hi, verdict}}}}. `compare old new`: refuses unless tasks and prompt fingerprints match (exit 2, naming the field), then prints, per arm present in both and per metric, new - old with a task-cluster bootstrap CI over the shared tasks, as `[agent-ab] compare arm=<a> metric=<m> diff=<d> ci=[lo,hi] verdict=<v>`. This is the call 0.5.5's proof makes.
7. test_score.py: canned sessions (a solved one, a partial, an empty patch, a contaminated one, a rename task, an insertion-only hunk) with hand-computed metrics; the --out-sessions / --from-metrics round trip giving an identical baseline; a network-terminated session excluded; bootstrap determinism; verdict direction per metric; compare refusing a mismatched fingerprint. `python3 test_score.py` exit 0.
8. README.md: the Scoring section (the metrics, the reading rule, compare).

1. cli/pyproject.toml (new): [build-system] requires = ["maturin>=1.7,<2.0"], build-backend = "maturin". [project] name = "glia-cli"; dynamic = ["version"]; description = "glia, the cross-language code-graph engine, as a command-line tool: find, blast-radius, trace, review and more over one graph of your repo."; readme = "README.md"; license = { file = "LICENSE" }; requires-python = ">=3.9"; authors as py/pyproject.toml; keywords ["code-graph", "cli", "static-analysis", "llm", "agents"]; classifiers (Environment :: Console, Programming Language :: Rust, Topic :: Software Development); [project.urls] as py/pyproject.toml. 2. cli/LICENSE: `cp LICENSE cli/LICENSE`; check-cli-wheel.sh fails when `cmp -s LICENSE cli/LICENSE` fails (as LICENSE and py/LICENSE are identical today).
