Preconditions: James's licence ruling (risks) is recorded in dev-notes/leap-054-packets.json `rulings` by the integrator before this packet is scheduled (a wave agent never waits on a mid-wave question; with no ruling recorded the packet is not scheduled); the packet quotes the ruling in its result; read the six repo-graph skills at that repo's HEAD (read-only) and skills/glia/SKILL.md at glia HEAD (after 0.5.3's EZ.1).
1. Each new SKILL.md (new): frontmatter `name: glia-<verb>` and a description carried over from repo-graph's with 'repo-graph' replaced by 'glia' where it names the engine, keeping the trigger phrases ('where is X', 'what breaks if I change this', ..). Body: one-line purpose; a `## Transports` section, identical in all six: 'Use whichever is available, in this order: the repo-graph MCP tools when loaded (`mcp__repo-graph__<tool>`, or `mcp__plugin_repo-graph_repo-graph__<tool>` from the Claude Code plugin; they may be deferred, so search your tool list first); the `glia` CLI when on PATH; else `uvx --from glia-cli glia ..` (no install; first run downloads the wheel); else `uvx mcp-repo-graph <verb>`. The MCP tools and `uvx mcp-repo-graph` print the same text; the glia CLI answers the same question with `--json` rows (`file`, `line`, tier).' Then a table `Want | MCP tool call | glia CLI | uvx mcp-repo-graph` and `## Steps` adapted from repo-graph's, each step naming the glia command too. Rows (glia column; repo `.` = the repo root):
   orient: overview -> `glia arch . --json` + `glia flows . --json`; blind spots -> `glia coverage . --json`; what could not be paired / looks dead -> `glia gaps . --json`; MCP `orient`, `orient seed=<node>`, `orient full=true` in their own column.
   find: a name / keyword -> `glia find . <text> --json`; the files a task is about -> `glia find . "<text>" --files --json` (0.5.3 EB.8); context for a task within a budget -> `glia pack . "<task>" --budget 4000 --json` (the concept / expand row); read -> 'open the file:line each row gives' (no glia verb).
   debug: a stacktrace / failing test / diff -> `glia resolve . "<signal>" --json` with `--kind` when the shape is known (values from cli/surface/resolve.txt); a diff -> `git diff > /tmp/d.diff && glia diff-impact . --diff /tmp/d.diff --json`; then `glia tests-for . <node> --json`.
   impact: one node -> `glia blast-radius . <node> --json`; the uncommitted change -> `glia diff-impact . --json`; a PR -> `glia review . --base main --title "<PR title>" --json` (EB.7); who implements / serves -> `glia implementors` / `glia serves`; plus the `⊘` / dead-code reading and 'check `glia coverage` before trusting a gap'.
   trace: a feature -> `glia trace . <feature> --json`; A to B -> `glia trace . <a> --to <b> --json` and `glia why . <a> <b> --json`; entry points -> `glia flows . --json`.
   init: build -> `glia build .`; history for co-change and the calibrated rankings -> `glia history sync .` then `glia history calibrate .` (EC.6); keep it fresh -> `glia install-hooks .` or `glia watch .`; MCP wiring -> `uvx mcp-repo-graph install` and the `.mcp.json` snippet (carried from repo-graph-init). Every flag used must exist in cli/surface/ at HEAD (the test enforces it); check `install-hooks` / `watch` / `history` argument shapes there.
   Each skill ends with the cross-links to its siblings (glia-find, glia-trace, ..) and to `glia` (the full CLI reference). Keep each <= 60 lines; no private-repo examples (use `UserService`, `/api/orders`, `checkout` as repo-graph does).
2. cli/tests/skill_surface.rs: (a) EXAMPLED gains six rows (its array length = the length at HEAD after 0.5.3's EZ.1, which may already have edited this file, plus six): glia-orient [arch, flows, coverage, gaps], glia-find [find, pack], glia-debug [resolve, diff-impact, tests-for], glia-impact [blast-radius, diff-impact, review], glia-trace [trace, why, flows], glia-init [] (build, history sync, install-hooks and watch take no --json at HEAD, cli/surface/*.txt), and because an empty row would let glia-init pass vacuously, add `const MIN_INVOCATIONS: [(&str, usize); 1] = [("glia-init", 3)]`: a skill listed there must yield at least that many checked invocations (asserted, documented in the module doc); (b) the command splitter treats a command whose words start `uvx --from <pkg>` (or `uvx --from=<pkg>`) followed by `glia` as a glia invocation of the rest, and documents that `uvx mcp-repo-graph ..` and MCP tool calls are repo-graph's surface, not checked here; (c) module doc and the fired_on line unchanged in form (`[skill] <name>: <n> invocations checked against cli/surface (<k> stale)`), now printing one line per skill directory (eight with HEAD's two). Unit tests in the file for the uvx prefix (`uvx --from glia-cli glia find . x --json` parsed as `find`; `uvx mcp-repo-graph find x` not parsed).
3. skills/LICENSE: if James rules the skills MIT (recommended, so repo-graph's MIT plugin can keep shipping a byte copy), write the MIT text (copyright 2026 James Chahwan); the SKILL.md files carry no licence text (frontmatter stays as Claude Code reads it) and README states 'skills/ is MIT (skills/LICENSE); the engine is the Glia Software License'. If he rules them under glia's LICENSE, do not create skills/LICENSE and README says the skills follow LICENSE.
4. README.md 'Use without MCP' paragraph: name the family (six task skills + `glia` + `glia-overlay`), the three transports, install by copying `skills/<name>/` to `~/.claude/skills/` or `<repo>/.claude/skills/`, the licence sentence, and that skill_surface checks the `glia` and `uvx --from glia-cli glia` forms.

packets.implementation:
One markdown doc (new), <= 120 lines, sections:
1. Question: do the answer rows an agent opened or acted on predict what later work touches, beyond commit history (co-change C0, 0.5.3 EA.3) and the 0.5.3 calibrated rankings?
2. What repo-graph would log (its MCP server, opt-in, local only, never uploaded): per tool call {ts, session id hash, tool, query text hash, glia version, rows returned [qname, file, rank]}; per subsequent agent action within the session {opened file, edited file, read node} joined to the row that named it (rank, tool); retention and redaction (no source text, hashes for query text; files are repo-relative paths). Where it lives (repo-graph's data dir, not .glia/), so no glia format changes.
3. The registered test (fixed before any data is read): units = sessions with >= 1 edit; signal U(file) = recency-weighted count of 'opened after being returned' events over earlier sessions of the same repo; task = rank the files a held-out session edits, given its first answer's seed files; rankers = the 0.5.3 calibrated pick (EC.8 / EC.13), C0, U, U blended with the calibrated pick (min-max mean, EB.2's fuse), and a control U~ with the same counts over files permuted within directory; metric recall@10 and MRR, paired by session, task-cluster bootstrap CI (FE.3's code); pass rule: blend - calibrated pick > 0 with the CI excluding 0 on at least 2 of 3 repos AND U - U~ > 0 (the signal is real, not popularity); minimum data: 200 sessions with edits per repo over >= 3 repos, public or aggregate-only.
4. What glia would build if it passes (a later leap; nothing in 0.5.4): a `use` snapshot step beside history sync (never inside a build) and one fusion candidate in the calibration bank, judged by the rank gate (EG.3).
5. What it costs repo-graph (the logging hook) and what it does NOT do (no telemetry off the machine, no ranking change before the test passes).
6. Status line: proposal; owner repo-graph; registration = a dated commit of this file plus repo-graph's acknowledgement; James decides whether to send it.
packets.acceptance: The file exists with the six sections; its pass rule names a metric, a control and a CI rule; `grep -n -i -E 'kina|quokka' dev-notes/use-signal-registered-test-0.5.4.md` prints nothing; no other file changes.
